fields.name: The LeBrun-Salamon conjecture: positive quaternionic-Kahler manifolds and contact Fano manifolds are homogeneous
fields.field: Differential and algebraic geometry; quaternionic-Kahler and contact Fano
fields.statement: A Riemannian manifold of dimension $4m$, $m\ge2$, is quaternionic-Kahler if its holonomy lies in $Sp(m)Sp(1)$; it is positive if its scalar curvature is positive. Wolf showed that the compact symmetric examples (the Wolf spaces) correspond to the adjoint varieties of simple complex Lie algebras, and Salamon's twistor construction attaches to every closed positive quaternionic-Kahler manifold a complex contact Fano manifold. LeBrun and Salamon proved finiteness and strong rigidity results and conjectured that the symmetric examples are the only ones. The algebraic form, the contact-Fano homogeneity conjecture, asks the same of every smooth complex projective contact Fano manifold, which should be an adjoint variety $\mathbb P(\mathcal O_{\min}(\mathfrak g))$. Known cases covered real dimension 8, 12 and 16 and low complex dimensions, or required extra hypotheses (reductive automorphism group, nonnegative sectional curvature). Is every closed connected positive quaternionic-Kahler manifold of dimension at least 8 a Wolf space, and is every contact Fano manifold an adjoint variety?
fields.posedBy: Claude LeBrun and Simon Salamon
fields.ageNote: LeBrun and Salamon, Strong rigidity of positive quaternion-Kahler manifolds, Invent. Math. 118 (1994), cited by the manuscript as the setting of the homogeneity conjecture; the general algebraic formulation is cited from Buczynski (Doc. Math. 2010, Conjecture 1.1).

fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: Theorem 1.1 and Corollaries 1.2-1.4 of the manuscript were read against the conjecture as posed. Theorem 1.1 states that every smooth connected complex projective contact Fano manifold of dimension $2n+1\ge3$ is contact-isomorphic to an adjoint variety; Corollary 1.4 deduces that every closed connected positive quaternionic-Kahler manifold of real dimension $4m\ge8$ is homothetic to a Wolf space. This is the conjecture in full. The proof (contact-line smoothing, a descended symmetric section on $X\times X$, a jet criterion for contact transitivity) was not refereed, and there is no Lean formalization. Readers should know that at least two earlier claimed proofs of the unrestricted classification (Yasukura's preprint versions, which the author later withdrew in part) did not survive, which the manuscript itself records.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: every smooth connected complex projective contact Fano manifold $(X,F)$ of dimension $2n+1$, $n\ge1$, is contact-isomorphic to the adjoint variety $Y_{\mathfrak g}$ of a simple complex Lie algebra, with $L\simeq\mathcal O(1)|_{Y_{\mathfrak g}}$. Corollaries: every such manifold is Kahler-Einstein; every smooth projective contact manifold with $b_2=1$ is an adjoint variety and with $b_2\ge2$ is $\mathbb P(T^*Z)$ (via Kebekus-Peternell-Sommese-Wisniewski and Demailly); every closed connected positive quaternionic-Kahler manifold of real dimension $4m\ge8$ satisfies $\nabla Rm=0$ and is homothetic to a Wolf space. It says nothing about negative or zero scalar curvature, about noncompact or incomplete metrics, or about compact Kahler contact manifolds that are not projective beyond the jet criterion it states.

fields.significanceNote: The LeBrun-Salamon conjecture has been a central open problem on special holonomy since 1994, with the algebraic contact-Fano form studied across algebraic geometry; known cases stopped at real dimension 16. Placed below Cannon's Conjecture (62) and the Yau Uniformization Conjecture (58), and above the Generator problem for von Neumann algebras (50).

fields.name: Katok's entropy rigidity conjecture in dimension at least three
fields.field: Smooth dynamics; geodesic flows in negative curvature
fields.statement: Let $(M,g)$ be a closed connected Riemannian manifold with strictly negative sectional curvature and geodesic flow $\phi_t$ on the unit tangent bundle. The variational principle gives $h_{m_L}(\phi_1)\le h_{top}(\phi_1)$, where $m_L$ is normalized Liouville measure. Katok (1982) proved for surfaces that equality forces constant curvature, and proved the higher-dimensional statement within the conformal class of a locally symmetric metric; later work gave only local rigidity near real or complex hyperbolic metrics. Katok conjectured that in every dimension equality of the Liouville entropy and the topological entropy characterizes locally symmetric metrics. Does $h_{m_L}=h_{top}$ hold for a negatively curved closed manifold only when $g$ is locally symmetric?
fields.posedBy: Anatole Katok
fields.ageNote: Katok, Entropy and closed geodesics, Ergodic Theory Dynam. Systems 2 (1982), p. 347, cited by the manuscript as the formulation; the surface case is proved there.
fields.aiRole: The release README says the results were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model with a fixed procedure, on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result, and that some outputs build on earlier model results. This result is not among the README's exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region). The manuscript is authored 'OpenAI' and names no human author. The family is a single manuscript (September 23, 2026).
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: Theorem 1.1 was read against Katok's conjecture. For $n\ge3$ and strictly negative sectional curvature it states $h_{m_L}(\phi_1)=h_{top}(\phi_1)$ if and only if $\nabla R=0$, that is, the universal cover is a rank-one symmetric space of noncompact type at some scale. This is the conjecture in all dimensions where it was open (Katok proved $n=2$). The proof derives global smoothness of the stable and unstable distributions from entropy equality via normal forms, formal symmetry algebras and quantitative realization, then applies Benoist-Foulon-Labourie; it was not refereed. There is no Lean formalization.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for a closed connected smooth Riemannian manifold of dimension $n\ge3$ with strictly negative sectional curvature, normalized Liouville measure has maximal entropy for the geodesic flow if and only if the metric is locally symmetric (real, complex, quaternionic or Cayley hyperbolic, any scale). When the metric is not locally symmetric, the measure of maximal entropy and Liouville measure are mutually singular. It does not treat nonpositive curvature, Anosov geodesic flows without negative curvature, or the related volume-entropy (Besson-Courtois-Gallot) setting.
fields.sourceName: OpenAI math release: Entropy equality and local symmetry in negative curvature
fields.significanceNote: Katok's conjecture has been the guiding rigidity question for geodesic flows since 1982, open in every dimension above two except near symmetric metrics. Placed below Sinai's standard map entropy conjecture (58) and Rokhlin's multiple-mixing problem (62), level with the Lipschitz isomorphism problem for separable Banach spaces (52).

fields.name: NP-hardness of approximating Uniform Sparsest Cut within every constant factor
fields.field: Hardness of approximation; graph partitioning
fields.statement: Uniform Sparsest Cut asks, for a graph on $N$ vertices with nonnegative capacities $c_{ij}$, for the minimum over nonempty proper $S$ of $\sum_{i\in S,j\notin S}c_{ij}/(|S|(N-|S|))$. Arora, Rao and Vazirani gave an $O(\sqrt{\log N})$ approximation. Exact computation is NP-hard, but approximation lower bounds were known only under assumptions: Ambuhl, Mastrolilli and Svensson ruled out a PTAS assuming SAT has no subexponential randomized algorithms, and the Small-Set Expansion hypothesis gives hardness of every constant factor. For the nonuniform problem, hardness of every constant factor follows from the Unique Games Conjecture. Is it NP-hard, with no unproved hypothesis, to approximate Uniform Sparsest Cut within some constant factor, or within every constant factor?
fields.posedBy: Open problem in the hardness-of-approximation literature; discussed by Ambuhl, Mastrolilli and Svensson and by Manurangsi and Trevisan
fields.ageNote: The manuscript gives no single posing reference. It cites Ambuhl-Mastrolilli-Svensson (SIAM J. Comput. 2011; FOCS 2007 version) for the strongest prior hardness and Manurangsi-Trevisan (APPROX 2018, Section 1.2) and d'Orsi et al. (2025) for the uniform versus nonuniform gap. The question is at least as old as the 2007 PTAS-hardness result.

The family has two manuscripts dated September 24, 2026: the hardness reduction (this entry) and a separate integrality-gap construction (its own entry).
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: Theorem 1.1 was read against the question. For every fixed $C>1$ it gives a polynomial-time reduction from 3CNF satisfiability to graphs with nonnegative rational capacities and unit demand on every pair, with $\Phi(G)\le a$ for satisfiable and $\Phi(G)>Ca$ for unsatisfiable formulas, using no unproved complexity hypothesis. That answers the question as posed (every constant factor, exact uniform demands, deterministic Karp reduction). The PCP-style proof (Garcia-Stichtenoth tower tests, rare-event extraction, cut-variance analysis) was not refereed and is not formalised; the Lean formalization in this family covers only the integrality-gap companion.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every fixed $C>1$ there is a polynomial-time reduction from 3SAT producing uniform-demand instances with a multiplicative gap $C$, so approximating Uniform Sparsest Cut within any constant factor is NP-hard. The constants and exponents of the reduction depend on $C$. It does not give a superconstant (for instance $\sqrt{\log N}$-type) hardness factor, does not address Balanced Separator directly, and says nothing about the Small-Set Expansion hypothesis itself.

fields.significanceNote: Unconditional constant-factor hardness for Uniform Sparsest Cut was a well-known open problem in approximation algorithms, with only conditional or PTAS-type lower bounds before. fields.name: The Goemans-Linial integrality gap for uniform sparsest cut is nearly square-root logarithmic
fields.shortName: Uniform sparsest cut SDP integrality gap
fields.field: Approximation algorithms; semidefinite relaxations and metric embeddings
fields.statement: The Goemans-Linial relaxation of uniform sparsest cut minimizes $\sum_{i<j}c_{ij}d(i,j)$ over negative-type semimetrics $d$ with $\sum_{i<j}d(i,j)=1$. Arora, Rao and Vazirani showed its integrality gap with uniform demands is $O(\sqrt{\log n})$. Devanur, Khot, Saket and Vishnoi refuted the conjecture that the uniform gap is bounded, with an $\Omega(\log\log n)$ lower bound, and Kane and Meka raised it to $\exp(\Omega(\sqrt{\log\log n}))$. For general demands the gap is $\Theta(\sqrt{\log n})$ up to lower-order factors (Naor-Young, Chang-Naor-Ren), but those constructions have constant average distortion and give nothing for uniform demands. What is the order of growth of the Goemans-Linial integrality gap for uniform sparsest cut, and does it reach $\sqrt{\log n}$?
fields.posedBy: Open after Arora, Rao and Vazirani (2004) and Devanur, Khot, Saket and Vishnoi (2006); see also Kane and Meka (2013)
fields.ageNote: The manuscript cites no explicit statement of the question. The uniform constant-gap conjecture was refuted by Devanur-Khot-Saket-Vishnoi (STOC 2006); the remaining question of the true order sits between their and Kane-Meka's lower bounds and the ARV $O(\sqrt{\log n})$ upper bound (first presented 2004).

fields.name: Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture for abstract elementary classes
fields.field: Model theory; abstract elementary classes
fields.statement: Morley proved that a countable first-order theory categorical in one uncountable cardinal is categorical in all of them. Shelah's abstract elementary classes (AECs) generalise elementary classes to nonelementary settings such as $L_{\omega_1,\omega}$ sentences, without compactness. Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture asks for an analogue: for each infinite cardinal $\lambda$ there should be a threshold $\mu(\lambda)$ such that every AEC $K$ with $LS(K)\le\lambda$ that is categorical in some cardinal $\ge\mu(\lambda)$ is categorical in every cardinal $\ge\mu(\lambda)$. Prior proofs needed amalgamation, tameness, a successor starting cardinal, large cardinals or weak GCH. Is eventual categoricity provable in ZFC for all AECs?
fields.posedBy: Saharon Shelah
fields.ageNote: The manuscript cites Shelah, Classification Theory for Abstract Elementary Classes (2009), Conjecture N.4.2, and Boney-Vasey (2015). The conjecture is older than that book: the companion notes Shelah introduced AECs in the mid-1970s with these categoricity questions, but the release gives no earlier dated statement.
fields.aiRole: The release README says the results were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model with a fixed procedure, on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result, and that some outputs build on earlier model results. This result is not among the README's exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region). The manuscript is authored 'OpenAI' and names no human author. The family has two manuscripts dated September 24, 2026: the ZFC eventual categoricity theorem (this entry) and a CH counterexample to the prescribed Hanf threshold (its own entry).
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: Theorem 1.2 was read against the conjecture. It gives, for every infinite $\lambda$, a cardinal $\mu(\lambda)$ such that every AEC with $LS(K)\le\lambda$ categorical in one cardinal $\ge\mu(\lambda)$ is categorical in all cardinals $\ge\mu(\lambda)$, in ZFC, with no amalgamation, joint embedding, tameness or no-maximal-models hypothesis and any starting cardinal. This is the qualitative conjecture. It does not give a numerical threshold. The long proof (order presentations, working schemes, geometry built from unbounded categoricity) was not refereed and is not formalised; the family's Lean formalization covers only the CH companion.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.2: for every infinite cardinal $\lambda$ there is $\mu(\lambda)\ge\lambda$ such that every AEC $K$ with $LS(K)\le\lambda$ categorical in some $\kappa\ge\mu(\lambda)$ is categorical in every $\kappa'\ge\mu(\lambda)$; equivalently (Theorem 1.3) an AEC categorical in unboundedly many cardinals is categorical on a tail. It applies to $L_{\omega_1,\omega}$ sentences in countable languages. It gives no explicit value for $\mu(\lambda)$; the prescribed $\beth_{\omega_1}$ threshold for $L_{\omega_1,\omega}$ and the Hanf threshold for AECs are left separate (the companion refutes the latter under CH).

fields.significanceNote: Eventual categoricity is the central test question of nonelementary model theory, open for decades and the target of the whole AEC program, though less known outside logic. Placed level with the Transitive Algebra Problem (46), below the Generator problem for von Neumann algebras (50), and above Wall's manifold-realization question for Poincare duality groups (42).

fields.name: The prescribed Hanf threshold in Shelah's categoricity conjecture is not provable in ZFC
fields.shortName: Prescribed categoricity threshold fails under CH
fields.field: Model theory; abstract elementary classes
fields.statement: For an abstract elementary class $K$ put $H(K)=\beth_{(2^{LS(K)})^+}$, the Hanf number for existence of arbitrarily large models. Beside the qualitative eventual categoricity conjecture, Shelah's program states a prescribed-threshold form: if $K$ is categorical in some $\lambda\ge H(K)$, then $K$ is categorical in every $\mu\ge H(K)$. Under amalgamation and tameness this transfer is known (Vasey), and a transfer at this bound for arbitrary AECs has been claimed (Espindola 2023). Grossberg distinguishes the prescribed and unspecified-threshold forms, and Saroch-Trlifaj (2024) give the exact formulation. Does categoricity above $H(K)$ always transfer to every cardinal at least $H(K)$, for arbitrary AECs?
fields.posedBy: Saharon Shelah (threshold form; formulated by Grossberg and by Saroch and Trlifaj)
fields.ageNote: The family cites Shelah 2009, Conjecture N.4.3(1)(b), for an explicit threshold, Grossberg's draft book (Conjectures 4.4-4.6) and Saroch-Trlifaj 2024 (Section 2.3) for the exact form refuted here.

The family has two manuscripts dated September 24, 2026: this CH construction and the ZFC eventual categoricity theorem (its own entry). This manuscript is the formalised one.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: Theorem 1.1 was read against the threshold form. Under CH it builds an AEC in a countable relational language with $LS(K)=\aleph_0$, two nonisomorphic models of size $\beth_{\omega_2}=H(K)$, and categoricity in every $\mu\ge\beth_{(2^{\aleph_1})^+}$; with Godel's consistency of CH the prescribed form is unprovable in ZFC if ZFC is consistent. It does not show the prescribed form false in ZFC. lean/formalization.yaml lists comparator CHObstruction, declaration OAI.CHObstruction.main; the statement was read here and asserts exactly Theorem 1.1, with the AEC axioms (coherence, chain unions over ordinals, LS bound) spelled out over ZFSet carriers. The nonprovability corollary is not formalised. Not rebuilt here. Permitted axioms: propext, Quot.sound, Classical.choice. The manuscript says its construction contradicts Espindola's published claim (Theorem 4.1) of transfer at this bound. Listed as Contested because of the conflicting claim described in the claim issue.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1 (assuming CH): there is an AEC $K$ in a countable finitary relational language with $LS(K)=\aleph_0$, at least two nonisomorphic models of cardinality $\beth_{\omega_2}=H(K)$, and categorical in every cardinal $\ge\Lambda=\beth_{(2^{\aleph_1})^+}$. So categoricity at $\Lambda^+$ does not transfer down to $H(K)$, and the prescribed-threshold form is not a theorem of ZFC (if ZFC is consistent). The same class is eventually categorical, so this is compatible with the qualitative conjecture. It does not decide whether the prescribed form can hold under other hypotheses (for example failure of CH), and it does not concern the $\beth_{\omega_1}$ threshold for $L_{\omega_1,\omega}$.

fields.name: Kobayashi's conjecture: a compact Kahler manifold with no entire curves has ample canonical bundle
fields.field: Complex geometry; Kobayashi hyperbolicity
fields.statement: A compact complex manifold $X$ is Kobayashi hyperbolic exactly when every holomorphic map $\mathbb C\to X$ is constant (Brody). Kobayashi conjectured that hyperbolicity forces positivity of the canonical bundle: a compact Kahler hyperbolic manifold should have ample $K_X$, and hence be projective. Known results needed metric hypotheses: negative or quasi-negative holomorphic sectional curvature (Wu-Yau, Tosatti-Yang, Diverio-Trapani), or Kahler hyperbolicity in Gromov's sense (Chen-Yang); without rational curves $K_X$ is known to be nef (Ou, Cao-Horing), but bigness was open. Is $K_X$ ample for every compact Kahler manifold of positive dimension that contains no nonconstant entire curve?
fields.posedBy: Shoshichi Kobayashi
fields.ageNote: Kobayashi, Hyperbolic Manifolds and Holomorphic Mappings (Marcel Dekker, 1970), cited by the manuscript as the source of the theory; Diverio's 2020 survey discusses the conjecture.
fields.aiRole: The release README says the results were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model with a fixed procedure, on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result, and that some outputs build on earlier model results. This result is not among the README's exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region). The manuscript is authored 'OpenAI' and names no human author. The family is a single manuscript (September 23, 2026). Its two corollaries cite other results from the same release (Fujita freeness and a semialgebraic-cover classification); the main theorem does not use them.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: Theorem 1.1 was read against Kobayashi's conjecture. It states that every compact connected Kahler manifold of positive dimension in which every holomorphic map from $\mathbb C$ is constant has ample $K_X$, so a power of $K_X$ embeds $X$ projectively. That is the conjecture in the smooth compact Kahler category. The proof (extremal holomorphic discs with an area penalty, a boundary-normalised frame, a Hessian identity giving a volume lower bound, then Aubin-Yau and Morse inequalities) was not refereed. There is no Lean formalization. The singular and non-Kahler settings are outside its scope, as the paper says.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: if $X$ is a compact connected Kahler manifold of positive dimension and every holomorphic map $\mathbb C\to X$ is constant, then $K_X$ is ample and $X$ is projective. Corollaries: $K_X^{\otimes m}$ is globally generated for $m\ge n+2$ (using the release's Fujita freeness result), and a finite cover splits as a ball-quotient-type factor times a hyperbolic factor when the universal cover is semialgebraic. It does not cover singular spaces, non-Kahler compact complex manifolds, or the converse direction (Green-Griffiths-Lang type statements).

fields.name: Ergodicity of billiards in every triangle with an irrational angle
fields.field: Ergodic theory; polygonal billiards
fields.statement: For a Euclidean triangle $Q$ with angles $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$, consider the unit-speed billiard flow on $Q\times S^1$ with specular reflection, discarding the null set of trajectories that hit a vertex, and the measure $dA\,d\theta/(2\pi\,\mathrm{Area}(Q))$. When all angles are rational multiples of $\pi$ the flow splits into invariant directional surfaces and is not ergodic. Zemlyakov-Katok's unfolding and Kerckhoff-Masur-Smillie gave ergodicity for a dense $G_\delta$ set of polygons, Vorobets for angles with exceptionally fast rational approximation, and Chaika-Forni weak mixing for a dense $G_\delta$ set; numerical studies of some irrational right and isosceles triangles even suggested nonergodicity. Is the billiard flow ergodic in every triangle with at least one angle irrational relative to $\pi$?
fields.posedBy: Classical problem of polygonal billiards (setting of Zemlyakov and Katok; surveyed by Masur and Tabachnikov)
fields.ageNote: The manuscripts cite no explicit posing statement or date. The question arises from Zemlyakov-Katok (1975) and Kerckhoff-Masur-Smillie (1986), whose generic results left individual irrational triangles open; Masur-Tabachnikov's 2002 survey is cited.
fields.aiRole: The release README says the results were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model with a fixed procedure, on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result, and that some outputs build on earlier model results. This result is not among the README's exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region). The manuscript is authored 'OpenAI' and names no human author. The family has two manuscripts: ergodicity (September 25, 2026, this entry's principal) and weak mixing (October 5, 2026), which extends the ergodicity paper's coefficient-energy method to eigenfunctions.

fields.name: The separable quotient problem for Banach spaces
fields.field: Banach space theory; set-theoretic functional analysis
fields.statement: Every infinite-dimensional Banach space has a separable infinite-dimensional closed subspace. The separable quotient problem asks for the dual statement: does every infinite-dimensional Banach space $X$ (real or complex) admit a bounded linear surjection onto a separable infinite-dimensional Banach space, equivalently a closed subspace $M$ with $X/M$ separable and infinite dimensional? Positive answers were known for separable spaces (Johnson-Rosenthal), dual spaces (Argyros-Dodos-Kanellopoulos), spaces of density below $\mathfrak b$ (Saxon-Sanchez Ruiz), and, consistently, densities at least $\aleph_\omega$ under large cardinals (Dodos-Lopez-Abad-Todorcevic). Does every infinite-dimensional Banach space have a separable infinite-dimensional quotient?
fields.posedBy: Traditionally attributed to Stefan Banach and Stanislaw Mazur; early written formulation by H. P. Rosenthal
fields.ageNote: The manuscript cites Brech (2025, p. 74): the problem is not stated explicitly in Banach's 1932 book, and Rosenthal's 1969 paper is an early written formulation. It is commonly dated to the 1930s by attribution.

fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: Theorem 1.1 was read against the problem. ZFC proves (i) if the continuum is real-valued measurable, every infinite-dimensional Banach space over $\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$ has a separable infinite-dimensional quotient, and (ii) under CH some space has none; hence independence relative to a measurable cardinal, and full independence for density $\aleph_1$ relative to ZFC. The challenge lean/ComparatorChallenges/SeparableQuotientNegative.json and its solution module OAI.Analysis.SeparableQuotients.Main exist at the pinned commit (found via lean/docs/323.md) but are not in the formalization catalogue. The statement was read here: CH implies the separable-quotient assertion fails over both $\mathbb R$ and $\mathbb C$. That is narrower than the headline: the positive direction and the independence conclusion are not formalised. Not rebuilt here. Permitted axioms: propext, Quot.sound, Classical.choice. The independence result is relative to the consistency of a measurable cardinal. Listed as Unreviewed rather than Lean-checked because its formal statement covers only one direction of the independence claim (CH implies a counterexample).
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for $\mathbb F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, ZFC proves that if $2^{\aleph_0}$ is real-valued measurable then every infinite-dimensional Banach space over $\mathbb F$ has a separable infinite-dimensional quotient, and that under CH there is a counterexample of density $\aleph_1$. So the problem is independent of ZFC if ZFC plus a measurable cardinal is consistent; restricted to density $\aleph_1$ it is independent relative to ZFC alone (Corollary 1.2, with Martin's axiom). It does not give a ZFC answer, does not remove the measurable-cardinal strength for the unrestricted statement, and leaves open which other axioms decide it.

fields.name: The Toms-Winter conjecture: strict comparison implies Jiang-Su stability for simple nuclear C*-algebras
fields.field: Operator algebras; regularity in the Elliott classification program
fields.statement: For simple separable unital infinite-dimensional nuclear C*-algebras $A$, the Toms-Winter conjecture asserts the equivalence of three regularity properties: finite nuclear dimension, Jiang-Su stability $A\cong A\otimes\mathcal Z$, and strict comparison of positive elements by traces. Winter and Castillejos-Evington-Tikuisis-White-Winter proved finite nuclear dimension equivalent to $\mathcal Z$-stability, and Rordam proved that $\mathcal Z$-stability gives strict comparison. The remaining implication, strict comparison implies $\mathcal Z$-stability, was known only under conditions on the tracial boundary (finitely many extreme traces, compact finite-dimensional boundary, Lin's condition) or with uniform property $\Gamma$. Does strict comparison imply $\mathcal Z$-stability for every simple separable nuclear non-elementary C*-algebra?
fields.posedBy: Andrew Toms and Wilhelm Winter
fields.ageNote: The release cites Winter-Zacharias, The nuclear dimension of C*-algebras (Adv. Math. 2010), Conjecture 9.3, and Schafhauser-Tikuisis-White's 99 problems (Conjecture 5, Problem XVIII). The conjecture circulated in Toms and Winter's work a few years earlier.

fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: Theorem 1.1 of the principal manuscript was read against the conjecture. It states that every separable simple nuclear non-elementary C*-algebra with strict comparison (in the extended-functional convention, which it shows equals almost unperforation of the Cuntz semigroup) is $\mathcal Z$-stable, including nonunital algebras with unbounded traces. With the known equivalence of finite nuclear dimension and $\mathcal Z$-stability this completes the conjecture. The tracial-projection companion proves the unital case independently. Separability and nuclearity remain hypotheses; nonnuclear and non-separable algebras are not treated.

fields.name: Robert-Tikuisis Conjecture (C1): finite nuclear dimension implies Jiang-Su stability without elementary subquotients
fields.field: Operator algebras; nuclear dimension of nonsimple C*-algebras
fields.statement: For simple algebras, finite nuclear dimension and Jiang-Su stability are equivalent away from the elementary case. Robert and Tikuisis studied the nonsimple setting, where the natural exclusion is that no ideal subquotient $I/J$ is a nonzero elementary algebra $\mathcal K(H)$ (nowhere scattered algebras). Their Conjecture (C1) predicts that a separable nuclear C*-algebra of finite nuclear dimension with no nonzero elementary ideal subquotients absorbs the Jiang-Su algebra $\mathcal Z$. Does finite nuclear dimension imply $A\cong A\otimes\mathcal Z$ for every separable nuclear C*-algebra with no elementary subquotients?

fields.ageNote: Robert and Tikuisis, Nuclear dimension and Z-stability of non-simple C*-algebras, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 369 (2017) (arXiv 2013), cited by the manuscript.

fields.name: Szabo's Conjecture A on equivariant Jiang-Su stability, in the unital stably finite case
fields.shortName: Szabo's Conjecture A, unital stably finite case
fields.field: Operator algebras; C*-dynamics of amenable group actions
fields.statement: Let $A$ be a separable simple nuclear C*-algebra with $A\cong A\otimes\mathcal Z$ and let $\alpha$ be an action of a countable discrete amenable group $G$ on $A$. Szabo's Conjecture A predicts automatic equivariant Jiang-Su stability: $\alpha$ should be cocycle conjugate to $\alpha\otimes\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal Z}$. Szabo proved it for finite algebras with finitely many rays of extremal traces and very weak comparison; the general case was open, in particular when the action moves traces. Is every amenable action on a separable simple nuclear $\mathcal Z$-stable C*-algebra equivariantly $\mathcal Z$-stable?
fields.posedBy: Gabor Szabo
fields.ageNote: Szabo, Equivariant property (SI) revisited, Anal. PDE 14 (2021), Conjecture A, cited by the manuscript.

fields.name: Schafhauser-Tikuisis-White Problem XXI: tracial real rank zero implies uniform property Gamma
fields.field: Operator algebras; uniform tracial completions
fields.statement: Let $A$ be a unital separable simple infinite-dimensional nuclear stably finite C*-algebra with traces, $B$ its uniform tracial completion, and $B^\omega$ the uniform tracial ultrapower along a free ultrafilter. Uniform property $\Gamma$ asks for central projections that halve every limit trace on every coefficient. Schafhauser, Tikuisis and White asked (Problem XXI, in their completion-and-halving formulation) whether real rank zero of $B^\omega$ forces uniform property $\Gamma$. Does real rank zero of the uniform tracial ultrapower imply uniform property $\Gamma$?
fields.posedBy: Christopher Schafhauser, Aaron Tikuisis and Stuart White
fields.ageNote: Schafhauser, Tikuisis and White, Nuclear C*-algebras: 99 problems (arXiv 2506.10902, 2025), Section 6, Problem XXI, Definition 16.

The statement was read here: for every separable, topologically simple, infinite-dimensional, nuclear (unique C*-norm on tensor products), stably finite unital C*-algebra with a tracial state, and every free ultrafilter at which the family ultrapower of the uniform tracial completion has real rank zero, there is a central projection halving every limit trace on every element of the completion. The claim is wrapped in existential quantifiers over five auxiliary construction classes (norms on quotients, null ideals, Cauchy algebras, limit traces), which the proof must supply. It states the headline of Problem XXI; the strict-comparison results of the same paper are not in this statement. Not rebuilt here. Permitted axioms: propext, Quot.sound, Classical.choice. fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for $A$ unital, separable, simple, infinite-dimensional, nuclear and stably finite with $T(A)\neq\emptyset$, if $B^\omega$ has real rank zero then there is a projection $p\in B^\omega\cap B'$ with $\lambda(px)=\lambda(x)/2$ for all $x\in B$ and all limit traces $\lambda$, so $A$ has uniform property $\Gamma$; it also identifies all traces on $B$. It does not show that real rank zero of $B^\omega$ holds in general, and Toms (2026) has shown nuclearity alone does not give uniform property $\Gamma$.

fields.name: Does the exact discrete Fourier transform require order n log n operations in unrestricted linear circuits?
fields.shortName: The n log n lower bound for the DFT
fields.field: Algebraic complexity; arithmetic circuits for the Fourier transform
fields.statement: The fast Fourier transform computes $F_n=(\zeta_n^{jk})$ with $O(n\log n)$ arithmetic operations, and no asymptotically faster method was known. Matching lower bounds were proved only in restricted models: Morgenstern for linear circuits with bounded coefficients, Ailon for unitary two-coordinate gates or bounded intermediate conditioning. In the unrestricted model, a linear circuit uses gates $u+v$, $u-v$ and $\lambda u$ with arbitrary fixed complex $\lambda$, each costing one, and must output $F_nx$ exactly for every $x$. Is the minimum size $L(n)$ of such a circuit at least $cn\log n$ for some $c>0$ and all large $n$, or can the Fourier transform be computed exactly with $o(n\log n)$ operations?
fields.posedBy: Long-standing open question in algebraic complexity; discussed by Ailon (2013) and Alman and Rao (2023)
fields.ageNote: The manuscripts give no posing date. They cite Ailon (2013, abstract) and Alman-Rao (2023, Section 1) for the question; the restricted lower bound it contrasts with is Morgenstern (1973).
fields.aiRole: The release README says the results were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model with a fixed procedure, on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result, and that some outputs build on earlier model results. This result is not among the README's exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region). The manuscript is authored 'OpenAI' and names no human author. The family has two manuscripts dated September 25, 2026: 'Finite tensor savings and exact Fourier circuits' (this entry's principal, nonuniform circuits along a subsequence) and 'An explicit power saving for the exact discrete Fourier transform' (a uniform algorithm at every length). The explicit-power-saving paper reuses a phase network from another release manuscript on integer multiplication.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: Theorem 1.1 of the principal manuscript was read against the question; it states $\liminf L(n)/(n\log_2 n)=0$ in the unrestricted model, refuting the lower bound. lean/formalization.yaml lists comparator ExactFourier, declaration OAI.ExactFourier.main_theorem. The statement was read here: for every $c>0$ and $N_0\ge2$ there are $n\ge N_0$ and a circuit (a DAG of add, subtract and scale-by-any-complex gates, outputs naming any available value) computing the unnormalised $F_n$ exactly with fewer than $cn\log_2 n$ gates. That is the headline claim. Not rebuilt here. Permitted axioms: propext, Quot.sound, Classical.choice. The model allows unbounded coefficients and conditioning, as the paper stresses; nothing is claimed for bit complexity or floating-point FFTs. The companion's every-length $O(n(\log n)^{1-10^{-13}})$ algorithm is not formalised.
fields.resultNote: Principal (Theorem 1.1): in exact complex linear circuits with arbitrary prechosen coefficients, $\liminf_n L(n)/(n\log_2 n)=0$, along lengths that are products of distinct primes, so the unrestricted $\Omega(n\log n)$ lower bound is false. Companion (Theorem 1.1): one deterministic algorithm computes $F_nx$ at every length in $O(n(\log n)^{\theta}(\log\log n)^{4-\theta})$ operations with $\theta<1-10^{-13}$, counting scalar preparation and indexing, given one specified root of unity. Neither result concerns bounded coefficients (where Morgenstern's bound stands), numerical stability, bit complexity or finite fields, and the constants are astronomically large.

fields.name: The Margulis-Platonov conjecture on normal subgroups of groups of rational points
fields.field: Algebraic groups over global fields; arithmetic groups
fields.statement: Let $G$ be an absolutely almost simple simply connected algebraic group over a global field $k$, let $A$ be the finite set of nonarchimedean places $v$ with $\mathrm{rank}_{k_v}G=0$, and let $\delta_A:G(k)\to\prod_{v\in A}G(k_v)$ be the diagonal map. The Margulis-Platonov conjecture asserts that the compact anisotropic local groups account for all abstract normal subgroups: every noncentral normal subgroup $N$ of $G(k)$ is $\delta_A^{-1}(W)$ for an open normal subgroup $W$. It was known for isotropic groups, inner type A (Segev-Seitz, Rapinchuk-Segev-Seitz) and most anisotropic types, leaving anisotropic outer A, trialitarian $D_4$ and $E_6$ cases over number fields. Is every noncentral normal subgroup of $G(k)$ of this form?
fields.posedBy: Grigory Margulis and Vladimir Platonov
fields.ageNote: The manuscript cites Margulis, Finiteness of quotient groups of discrete subgroups (Funct. Anal. Appl. 13, 1979), Section 2.4.8 of the Russian original, for the formulation, which grew from Kneser's and Platonov's simplicity questions.

The function-field companion's abstract states the same over every global function field. Neither proof was refereed; there is no Lean formalization. With Rapinchuk's theorem it gives the congruence subgroup property for $S$ of positive Dirichlet density in the split places. The October 5 companion proves the same over every global function field, including characteristic two. It does not settle Serre's congruence subgroup conjecture for finite $S$ or arbitrary infinite $S$.

fields.name: The generalized Cartan-Hadamard isoperimetric conjecture
fields.field: Riemannian geometry; isoperimetric inequalities
fields.statement: Let $(M^n,g)$ be a Cartan-Hadamard manifold: complete, simply connected, with sectional curvature $\le\kappa\le0$. The Euclidean Cartan-Hadamard conjecture (usually attributed to Aubin, also to Gromov and to Burago-Zalgaller) asserts that every bounded smooth domain $\Omega\subset M$ satisfies the Euclidean isoperimetric inequality $|\partial\Omega|\ge n\omega_n^{1/n}|\Omega|^{(n-1)/n}$, with equality only for regions isometric to Euclidean balls. Its generalized form replaces the right side by the boundary area of the equal-volume geodesic ball in the simply connected space form of curvature $\kappa$. It was known in dimension two (Weil, Beckenbach-Rado, Bol), three (Kleiner) and, for $\kappa=0$, four (Croke). Does the comparison with the model ball of curvature $\kappa$ hold in every dimension?
fields.posedBy: Thierry Aubin (Euclidean form, 1976); the curvature-kappa generalization is usually credited to Gromov and to Burago-Zalgaller
fields.ageNote: The manuscript does not attribute the conjecture; it cites Aubin's 1976 paper 'Problemes isoperimetriques et espaces de Sobolev' (the paper usually credited with the conjecture) only for the sharp Sobolev constant. The attribution and year come from the standard literature, not from this manuscript.

The Lean work covers the companion, not the principal manuscript. lean/docs/337.md points to two challenges, ComparatorChallenges/SharpCAT0Filling.json (theorem OAI.CAT0Fillings.sharp_integral_filling, solution module OAI.Geometry.CAT0Fillings.Main) and FillingCoefficient.json (OAI.SharpIntegralFillings.coefficient_optimal, module OAI.Geometry.IntegralFillings.Main); both solution files exist at the pinned commit, and neither challenge is in the formalization catalogue formalization.yaml. Corollaries give Faber-Krahn and Saint-Venant comparisons with the model ball. Equality rigidity for $\kappa<0$ is not claimed. The companion proves the sharp Euclidean filling bound for integral $n$-cycles, $n\ge2$, in any proper CAT(0) space and deduces the Euclidean inequality for domains in dimension $d\ge3$. Recent preprints cited by the paper (Chen-Ghomi-Wang, dimensions 3 to 9) overlap in low dimensions.

fields.name: Explicit depth-three circuit lower bounds beyond the square-root exponent
fields.field: Circuit complexity; depth-three Boolean circuits
fields.statement: For a Boolean function $f$ on $\{0,1\}^n$, let $S_3(f)$ be the least number of gates in an unbounded fan-in OR-AND-OR (depth-three) circuit computing $f$. Hastad's switching lemma gives $S_3(\text{parity})=2^{\Theta(\sqrt n)}$, and Paturi-Pudlak-Zane's bound $\Omega(n^{1/4}2^{\sqrt n})$ is tight for parity; all lower bounds for explicit functions remained of the form $2^{c\sqrt n}$ for a constant $c$. Hastad, Jukna and Pudlak asked for an explicit function needing $2^{n^{1/2+\varepsilon}}$ gates, and Gurumukhani-Paturi-Pudlak-Saks-Talebanfard discuss as open the weaker goal of a superconstant multiple of $\sqrt n$ in the exponent. Is there an explicit function, for instance a language in polynomial time, with $S_3(f_n)\ge 2^{\omega(\sqrt n)}$?

fields.name: No bigeodesics in planar first-passage percolation under a minimum-of-four second-moment condition
fields.field: First-passage percolation; infinite geodesics
fields.statement: Give the nearest-neighbor edges of $\mathbb Z^2$ i.i.d. nonnegative weights with a continuous law and let $T(x,y)$ be the passage-time metric. A bigeodesic is a doubly infinite path $(v_i)_{i\in\mathbb Z}$ every finite segment of which is a geodesic. Furstenberg asked, as recorded by Kesten (1986, Remark 9.22), whether such paths can exist; the planar no-bigeodesics conjecture (Damron-Hanson, Conjecture 1) asserts that almost surely there are none for i.i.d. continuous weights. Earlier results excluded bigeodesics only in fixed directions, under curvature or differentiability assumptions on the limit shape, or in restricted geodesic graphs. Is it true that almost surely planar first-passage percolation with i.i.d. continuous weights has no bigeodesic?

fields.name: Strict convexity and differentiability of the planar first-passage limit shape for exponential weights
fields.field: First-passage percolation; limit shapes
fields.statement: For i.i.d. edge weights on $\mathbb Z^2$, the Cox-Durrett shape theorem gives a norm $\mu$ with $T(0,\lfloor tv\rfloor)/t\to\mu(v)$ and a convex limit shape $\mathcal B=\{\mu\le1\}$. It is conjectured that for continuous weight laws $\mathcal B$ is strictly convex (no flat faces) and that $\mu$ is differentiable away from the origin (no corners); see the survey of Auffinger, Damron and Hanson. Neither property was known for any continuous law, including the exponential law, where the model coincides with the Eden-Richardson growth model. Partial results covered laws with an atom at the minimum (Marchand; Auffinger-Damron) and sufficient conditions (Lalley). For i.i.d. exponential edge weights, is the limit shape strictly convex with a $C^1$ boundary?

fields.name: The Shafarevich conjecture on holomorphic convexity of universal covers
fields.field: Complex algebraic geometry; universal covers and fundamental groups
fields.statement: Shafarevich asked whether the universal cover of a complete algebraic variety is holomorphically convex. In the usual smooth projective formulation: for every smooth connected projective complex variety $X$, is the universal cover $\widetilde X$, with the lifted complex structure, holomorphically convex, i.e. is the holomorphic hull $\{v:|g(v)|\le\sup_K|g|\ \forall g\in\mathcal O(\widetilde X)\}$ of every compact $K$ compact? A direct form for varieties with large fundamental group (Kollar) asks whether $\widetilde X$ is Stein when it contains no positive-dimensional compact analytic subvariety. The conjecture was proved for elliptic surfaces, for virtually nilpotent fundamental groups, and for fundamental groups with a faithful linear representation (Eyssidieux-Katzarkov-Pantev-Ramachandran). Does it hold in general?

fields.name: Banach's problem: a probability-preserving transformation with simple Lebesgue spectrum
fields.field: Ergodic theory; spectral theory of measure-preserving maps
fields.statement: For an invertible measure-preserving transformation $T$ of a probability space, the Koopman operator $U_Tg=g\circ T$ is unitary on $L^2$ and leaves the constants invariant. Banach's problem, in its probability-preserving form, asks whether some $T$ has simple Lebesgue spectrum on the orthogonal complement $L^2_0$ of the constants: equivalently, whether there is $f\in L^2_0$ whose iterates $\{f\circ T^n\}_{n\in\mathbb Z}$ form an orthonormal basis of $L^2_0$. Rokhlin (1949) asked for ergodic automorphisms with simple, or at least finite-multiplicity, Lebesgue spectrum. Known constructions gave Lebesgue components, finite-measure flows, simple non-Lebesgue spectrum, or infinite-measure examples, but not this. Does such a probability-preserving transformation exist?

fields.name: Wall's D(2) problem
fields.field: Algebraic topology; homotopy types of 2-complexes
fields.statement: A finite connected CW complex $X$ with fundamental group $G$ satisfies the $D(2)$ condition if $H_i(\widetilde X;\mathbb Z)=0$ for $i>2$ and $H^3(X;M)=0$ for every finitely generated $\mathbb ZG$-module $M$. Stably the answer is yes (Cohen), and it is yes for many finite groups (Johnson, Hambleton, Hofmann-Nicholson); candidate counterexamples (Cohen-Dyer, Bridson-Tweedale) stayed unresolved or conditional on relation-gap assertions. fields.name: The finitistic dimension conjecture for finite-dimensional algebras
fields.field: Representation theory of finite-dimensional algebras; homological algebra
fields.statement: For a finite-dimensional algebra $A$ over a field, the little finitistic dimension is $\mathrm{findim}\,A=\sup\{\mathrm{pd}_AN: N\text{ finitely generated},\ \mathrm{pd}_AN<\infty\}$. The finitistic dimension conjecture, publicized by Bass, asserts that $\mathrm{findim}\,A<\infty$ for every finite-dimensional (more generally, Artin) algebra. It was proved for monomial algebras, radical-cube-zero algebras and representation dimension at most three (Igusa-Todorov), and it implies several other homological conjectures; Huisgen-Zimmermann showed the little and big dimensions can differ but both stayed finite in all examples. fields.name: The asymptotic Gotsman-Linial conjecture on average sensitivity of polynomial threshold functions
fields.field: Analysis of Boolean functions; polynomial threshold functions
fields.statement: A degree-$d$ polynomial threshold function on $\{-1,1\}^n$ is $f(x)=\mathrm{sgn}(p(x))$ for a real polynomial $p$ of degree at most $d$. Its average sensitivity (total influence) is $I(f)=\sum_{i=1}^n\Pr[f(X)\ne f(X^{\oplus i})]$ for uniform $X$. Gotsman and Linial proposed that the maximum of $I(f)$ over degree-$d$ PTFs is attained by a symmetric function of $x_1+\dots+x_n$, which would give $I(f)=O(d\sqrt n)$; Chapman disproved the exact extremal form and separated it from the asymptotic bound. The best bounds were sublinear for fixed $d$ (Harsha-Klivans-Meka, Diakonikolas-Raghavendra-Servedio-Tan) and $\sqrt n(\log n)^{O(d\log d)}2^{O(d^2\log d)}$ (Kane). Is $I(f)=O(d\sqrt n)$ for every degree-$d$ polynomial threshold function, with an absolute constant?
fields.posedBy: Craig Gotsman and Nathan Linial (exact extremal form); asymptotic form stated by Chapman
fields.ageNote: Gotsman and Linial, Spectral properties of threshold functions (Combinatorica 1994, Section 5, p. 47), as cited by the manuscript. The asymptotic O(d sqrt n) form is stated as a separate conjecture by Chapman (2018, Conjectures 1.1-1.2) after the exact form was refuted.

fields.field: Geometric Langlands program; l-adic sheaves in positive characteristic
fields.statement: Let $X$ be a smooth projective connected curve over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$, $G$ a connected reductive group, $\ell\ne p$. Gaitsgory and Raskin constructed, under the characteristic hypotheses of the restricted theory of Arinkin-Gaitsgory-Kazhdan-Raskin-Rozenblyum-Varshavsky, a $\mathrm{QCoh}(Y)$-linear equivalence from $\mathrm{Shv}_{\mathrm{Nilp}}(\mathrm{Bun}_G(X))$ onto $\mathrm{IndCoh}_{\mathrm{Nilp}}(Y')$ for an open-and-closed union $Y'$ of connected components of the restricted stack $Y=\mathrm{LS}^{\mathrm{restr}}_{\check G}(X)$, and proved $Y'=Y$ for $GL_n$. Their Conjecture 1.3.10 asserts that no component is missing. Is $Y'=Y$, so that the restricted Langlands functor is an equivalence onto all of $\mathrm{IndCoh}_{\mathrm{Nilp}}(Y)$?

fields.ageNote: Gaitsgory-Raskin, Geometric Langlands in positive characteristic from characteristic zero, arXiv:2508.02237 (2025), Conjecture 1.3.10, as cited by the manuscript.

fields.resultNote: Theorem (full support): under either regime, $Y'=Y$, so $\mathbb L^{\mathrm{restr}}_G:\mathrm{Shv}_{\mathrm{Nilp}}(\mathrm{Bun}_G(X))\to\mathrm{IndCoh}_{\mathrm{Nilp}}(Y)$ is a $\mathrm{QCoh}(Y)$-linear equivalence; a rational-coefficient form is also proved over $\overline{\mathbb F}_q$. Consequences: nonzero localized categories at every spectral component, the full arithmetic trace formula in the finite-field regime, and nonzero Hecke eigenobjects for every parameter. It does not remove the characteristic hypotheses, and does not assert bounded constructibility or perversity of eigenobjects (the three October 5 eigensheaf companions construct perverse tame eigensheaves in specific settings).

fields.name: The Gaitsgory-Lafforgue-Raskin Ramanujan-Arthur decomposition of cuspidal automorphic functions over function fields
fields.field: Automorphic forms over function fields; Arthur parameters
fields.statement: Let $F$ be the function field of a smooth projective geometrically connected curve over $\mathbb F_q$, $G$ a split connected semisimple group, and $C_{\mathbb Q}$ the space of rational-valued cuspidal functions on $G(F)\backslash G(\mathbb A_F)/G(\mathcal O_{\mathbb A})$. For a nilpotent orbit $\mathcal O$ of the dual group with Jacobson-Morozov map $\phi_{\mathcal O}$, let $C_{\mathcal O}$ be the functions whose Hecke eigenvalues at every place $x$ have Satake class in $q_x^{1/2}$-twisted $\phi_{\mathcal O}$ times a compact element of the centralizer, the same orbit at every place. Gaitsgory, Lafforgue and Raskin conjectured (Conjectures 3.4.5 and 3.4.6, the rational and the $\ell$-adic Ramanujan-Arthur conjecture) that the cuspidal space decomposes accordingly. Is $\bigoplus_{\mathcal O}C_{\mathcal O}=C$?

fields.name: Rationality of the Gaitsgory-Lafforgue-Raskin canonical Arthur filtration
fields.shortName: Rationality of the canonical Arthur filtration
fields.field: Automorphic functions over function fields; geometric Langlands
fields.statement: For a split connected semisimple group $G$ over $\mathbb F_q$ and a curve $X$, Gaitsgory, Lafforgue and Raskin define a canonical filtration, indexed by nilpotent orbits of the dual Lie algebra, on the space of finitely supported unramified automorphic functions with $\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell$ coefficients, using singular support of $\ell$-adic sheaves and the trace of Frobenius. fields.name: The generalized Ramanujan conjecture for globally generic cuspidal representations of exceptional groups over function fields
fields.field: Automorphic representations over function fields; temperedness
fields.statement: Let $F$ be the function field of a curve over $\mathbb F_q$ and $G$ a split connected reductive group. The generalized Ramanujan conjecture, in its generic form (within Arthur's framework; see Shahidi), predicts that every globally generic cuspidal automorphic representation $\pi=\bigotimes'_v\pi_v$ of $G(\mathbb A_F)$ is tempered at every place $v$. Over function fields this was known for $GL_2$ (Drinfeld), $GL_n$ (L. Lafforgue), and split classical and quasi-split unitary groups (Lomeli); for exceptional groups only conditional unramified results (Sawin-Templier, Ciubotaru-Harris) were available. For split adjoint groups of type $G_2,F_4,E_6,E_7,E_8$ over a global function field, is every globally generic cuspidal automorphic representation tempered at every place?

fields.name: Critical two-point decay $r^{-1/4}(\log r)^{1/8}$ in the planar XY model
fields.shortName: XY critical decay with log correction
fields.field: Statistical mechanics; Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless transition
fields.statement: The nearest-neighbor XY model on $\mathbb Z^2$ at inverse temperature $b$ gives angles $\theta_x$ the weight $\exp(b\sum_{x\sim y}\cos(\theta_x-\theta_y))$. Berezinskii, Kosterlitz and Thouless predicted a transition at $b_c$ driven by vortex unbinding, with algebraic decay of the spin correlation $C_b(r)=\langle\cos(\theta_0-\theta_{re_1})\rangle$ for $b\ge b_c$. Kosterlitz's 1974 renormalization-group analysis predicts at criticality the universal exponent $\eta=1/4$ with a multiplicative logarithmic correction, $C_{b_c}(r)\asymp r^{-1/4}(\log r)^{1/8}$ (as recorded, e.g., by Janke for the Villain model). Rigorous work gave power-law bounds (McBryan-Spencer, Frohlich-Spencer, van Engelenburg-Lis) but not the critical exponent. Does $C_{b_c}(r)=B\,r^{-1/4}(\log r)^{1/8}(1+o(1))$ hold with $0<B<\infty$?
fields.posedBy: J. M. Kosterlitz (renormalization-group prediction), building on Berezinskii and Kosterlitz-Thouless
fields.ageNote: Kosterlitz, The critical properties of the two-dimensional XY model, J. Phys. C 7 (1974), cited by the manuscript; it also cites Janke (1997) for the explicit form with the logarithmic factor. Berezinskii (1971) and Kosterlitz-Thouless (1973) predicted the phase.

fields.name: The Kosterlitz essential singularity of the XY correlation length
fields.field: Statistical mechanics; Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless transition
fields.statement: For the nearest-neighbor XY model on $\mathbb Z^2$, let $m(b)$ be the exponential decay rate of the spin correlation along an axis and $\xi(b)=1/m(b)$ the correlation length, finite for $b<b_c$. Unlike ordinary critical points, where $\xi$ diverges as a power of $b_c-b$, Kosterlitz's renormalization-group analysis predicts an essential singularity: $\log\xi(b)\sim A/\sqrt{b_c-b}$ as $b\uparrow b_c$. Rigorous work established the transition and the exponential-versus-polynomial dichotomy (Frohlich-Spencer, van Engelenburg-Lis, Aizenman-Harel-Peled-Shapiro, Lammers) but not the rate of divergence. Is there a constant $A\in(0,\infty)$ with $\sqrt{b_c-b}\,\log\xi(b)\to A$ as $b\uparrow b_c$?
fields.posedBy: J. M. Kosterlitz
fields.ageNote: Kosterlitz, The critical properties of the two-dimensional XY model, J. Phys. C 7 (1974), cited by the manuscript as the source of the prediction.

It does not cover other lattices, the Villain model, the behaviour of the susceptibility, or corrections beyond the leading order.

fields.name: Almost everywhere convergence of Fourier series in L log L
fields.shortName: Fourier convergence in L log L
fields.field: Harmonic analysis; pointwise convergence of Fourier series
fields.statement: For an integrable function $f$ on the circle $\mathbb T$ let $S_Nf(x)=\sum_{|k|\le N}\widehat f(k)e^{ikx}$. Carleson (1966) proved $S_Nf\to f$ almost everywhere for $f\in L^2$, Hunt (1968) extended this to $L^p$, $p>1$, and Kolmogorov (1923) gave an integrable function whose Fourier series diverges almost everywhere. Between these, convergence was known in $L\log L\log\log L$ (Sjolin 1969), in $L\log L\log\log\log L$ (Antonov 1996) and in the quasi-Banach space $\mathrm{QA}$ of Arias de Reyna. Does $S_Nf(x)\to f(x)$ for almost every $x$, along the full sequence $N=0,1,2,\ldots$, for every $f$ in the Orlicz class $L\log L(\mathbb T)=\{f:\int|f|\log(2+|f|)<\infty\}$?
fields.posedBy: Classical question after Carleson, Hunt, Sjolin and Antonov; stated as Conjecture 1 (with a weak-L1 maximal formulation) by Victor Lie (2017)
fields.ageNote: The manuscript cites no first posing. The earliest explicit statement it cites is V. Lie, Pointwise convergence of Fourier series (I), JEMS 19 (2017), Definition 1.1 and Conjecture 1. The question is implicit in the work it lists from Sjolin (1969) and Antonov (1996) onward; the original posing date is not given in the literature read here.

A corollary also gives the Luxemburg-norm weak-$L^1$ maximal bound via Stein's theorem. The proof (an entropy-compression argument for a dyadic model, transferred to Fourier sums by dyadic representation of the Hilbert kernel) was not refereed. The key estimate is a good-set bound $\int_{\{M\rho\le e^{4h}\}}\sup_N|S_N\rho|\le Cd$ for bounded densities of height $e^d$, summed over height layers. The paper also deduces a weak-$L^1$ maximal inequality in Luxemburg norm. It does not address spaces strictly between $L\log L$ and $L^1$ (where Konyagin's divergence results apply below $L\sqrt{\log L}$), nor lacunary or higher-dimensional analogues.

fields.name: De Giorgi's conjecture on monotone solutions of the Allen-Cahn equation
fields.field: Elliptic PDE; Allen-Cahn equation and phase transitions
fields.statement: De Giorgi conjectured in 1978 that if $u\in C^2(\mathbb R^n)$ solves the Allen-Cahn equation $\Delta u=u^3-u$ with $|u|\le1$ and $\partial_{x_n}u>0$ everywhere, then for $n\le8$ the level sets of $u$ are hyperplanes, i.e. $u(x)=\tanh((e\cdot x-c)/\sqrt2)$ for a unit vector $e$ and $c\in\mathbb R$. It is the phase-transition analogue of the Bernstein problem for minimal graphs. Ghoussoub-Gui proved it for $n=2$, Ambrosio-Cabre for $n=3$, Savin for $4\le n\le8$ under the extra assumption that $u(x',t)\to\pm1$ as $t\to\pm\infty$, and del Pino-Kowalczyk-Wei gave counterexamples for $n\ge9$. Is every such monotone solution one-dimensional in every dimension $n\le8$, without the limit assumption?
fields.posedBy: Ennio De Giorgi
fields.ageNote: Stated at the International Meeting on Recent Methods in Nonlinear Analysis, Rome 1978; proceedings published by Pitagora, Bologna, 1979, as cited by the manuscript.

The paper states only the dimension-eight case; the lower dimensions $n\le7$ follow by extending a solution constantly in the missing variables, an observation made here, not in the paper. The proof reduces the monotone case to Theorem 1.2 (every stable solution on $\mathbb R^7$ is constant or planar, with no energy-growth hypothesis) using classical inputs (Alberti-Ambrosio-Cabre, Jerison-Monneau, Federer, Wang's near-unit-density theorem); the stable classification is the new part. A final section explains why the argument fails in dimension nine, consistent with del Pino-Kowalczyk-Wei. fields.name: The Sakoda-Sipser problem: exponential cost of simulating nondeterministic automata by two-way deterministic ones
fields.field: Automata theory; descriptional (state) complexity
fields.statement: Sakoda and Sipser (STOC 1978) asked how many states a two-way deterministic finite automaton (2DFA) needs to simulate an $n$-state one-way or two-way nondeterministic automaton (1NFA, 2NFA). The best known simulations are exponential, and they showed that the family $B_h$ (one-way liveness: words of binary relations on an $h$-element set whose product is nonempty) is complete for the one-way case. Exponential lower bounds were known only for restricted deterministic targets (Sipser's sweeping automata, Kapoutsis's few-reversal machines), and against unrestricted 2DFAs only quadratic bounds were known. Is there a polynomial $p$ such that every $n$-state 1NFA, or 2NFA, over any finite alphabet has an equivalent 2DFA with at most $p(n)$ states?

fields.name: Polynomial complementation of two-way nondeterministic finite automata
fields.field: Automata theory; descriptional (state) complexity
fields.statement: A two-way nondeterministic finite automaton (2NFA) has one read-only head moving in both directions between endmarkers. fields.name: Does the Partition Principle imply the Axiom of Choice?
fields.field: Set theory; choice principles and symmetric models
fields.statement: The Partition Principle (PP) says that whenever there is a surjection from a set $X$ onto a set $Y$, there is an injection from $Y$ into $X$; equivalently every partition of a set injects into the set. Over ZF the Axiom of Choice implies PP, and PP implies choice for well-orderable families. The converse is the old question: does PP imply AC over ZF? Equivalently, is ZF + PP + $\neg$AC consistent relative to ZF?

It also notes that Gilson's September 2026 corrections withdrew three earlier claimed constructions.

fields.name: Toda's Gepner conjecture for the quintic threefold
fields.field: Algebraic geometry; Bridgeland stability conditions on Calabi-Yau threefolds
fields.statement: Let $X\subset\mathbb P^4$ be a smooth complex quintic threefold and $\Phi=T_{\mathcal O_X}\circ(-\otimes\mathcal O_X(1))$, the composite of tensoring by the hyperplane bundle and the Seidel-Thomas spherical twist at $\mathcal O_X$, which satisfies $\Phi^5\simeq[2]$. Physics predicts a stability condition at the Gepner point of the stringy Kahler moduli space fixed by this symmetry. Toda (2013) conjectured, in normalized form, that there is a Bridgeland stability condition $\sigma=(Z,\mathcal P)$ on $D^b(\mathrm{Coh}\,X)$ with $Z(\Phi E)=e^{2\pi i/5}Z(E)$ and $\Phi\mathcal P(\varphi)=\mathcal P(\varphi+2/5)$, and reduced it to a strong Bogomolov-Gieseker type inequality. Does every smooth quintic threefold admit such a Gepner-type stability condition?
fields.posedBy: Yukinobu Toda
fields.ageNote: Toda, Gepner type stability conditions on graded matrix factorizations (arXiv 1302.6293, Conjecture 1.2) and Gepner point and strong Bogomolov-Gieseker inequality for quintic 3-folds (arXiv 1305.0345, Conjecture 3.1), as cited.

fields.name: Shub's entropy conjecture for C1 self-maps
fields.field: Smooth dynamical systems; topological entropy and homology
fields.statement: For a continuous self-map $f$ of a compact manifold $M$, let $h_{\mathrm{top}}(f)$ be its topological entropy and $\rho(f_*)$ the spectral radius of the induced map on real homology $H_*(M;\mathbb R)$. fields.name: The Blaschke conjecture: Blaschke manifolds are compact rank-one symmetric spaces
fields.field: Riemannian geometry; manifolds all of whose geodesics are closed
fields.statement: A connected closed Riemannian manifold $(M,g)$ of positive dimension is a Blaschke manifold if its injectivity radius equals its diameter, so every unit-speed geodesic minimizes up to the diameter. Round spheres, the real, complex and quaternionic projective spaces and the Cayley plane with their standard metrics are Blaschke. Blaschke posed the problem for surfaces (settled by Green, 1963); the sphere and real projective cases were settled by Berger, Kazdan, Weinstein and Yang, and Bott-Samelson theory fixes the cohomology type, but the metric question was open for the complex, quaternionic and Cayley types. Is every Blaschke manifold isometric, up to scaling, to a compact rank-one symmetric space?

fields.ageNote: Blaschke's Vorlesungen uber Differentialgeometrie I (1921) for surfaces; the higher-dimensional metric conjecture is as described in Besse, Manifolds all of whose geodesics are closed (1978), with McKay's 2016 progress summary, all cited by the manuscript.

fields.name: The strong thin tree conjecture
fields.field: Graph theory; spanning trees, cuts and connectivity
fields.statement: A spanning tree $T$ of a multigraph $G$ is $\alpha$-thin if $|\delta_T(S)|\le\alpha|\delta_G(S)|$ for every nonempty proper vertex set $S$. Goddyn's thin tree conjecture asks whether for every $\varepsilon>0$ sufficiently high edge connectivity guarantees an $\varepsilon$-thin spanning tree; the strong form asks for the rate: is there a universal constant $C$ such that every $k$-edge-connected multigraph has a $C/k$-thin spanning tree? Known results gave $O(1/k)$ for planar and bounded-genus graphs (Oveis Gharan-Saberi) and $\mathrm{poly}(\log\log n)/k$ in general (Anari-Oveis Gharan). Via Asadpour et al., thin trees bound the integrality gap of asymmetric TSP. Does every $k$-edge-connected finite multigraph have a spanning tree that is $C/k$-thin, with $C$ absolute?

fields.name: The Lipman-Zariski conjecture in characteristic zero
fields.field: Algebraic geometry; singularities and derivation modules
fields.statement: On a smooth complex variety of dimension $d$ the tangent sheaf is locally free of rank $d$. Lipman (1965), following a question of Zariski, proved that local freeness of the derivation module forces normality and asked for the converse of smoothness: if $A$ is a finitely generated integral $\mathbb C$-algebra and $\mathrm{Der}_{\mathbb C}(A)$ is locally free, is $A$ regular? It was known for hypersurfaces, local complete intersections, graded rings, isolated singularities in dimension at least three, klt and log canonical spaces, and several classes of normal surface singularities, but the surface case was open. Is every complex algebraic variety with locally free tangent sheaf nonsingular?

fields.name: Universal optimality of the triangular lattice in the plane (Cohn-Kumar)
fields.shortName: Universal optimality of the triangular lattice
fields.field: Discrete geometry; energy minimization and universal optimality
fields.statement: For a locally finite configuration $\mathcal C\subset\mathbb R^2$ of density one and a potential $g$, the energy per point is the lower limit of $N_R^{-1}\sum_{x\ne y\in\mathcal C\cap B_R}g(|x-y|^2)$. Among lattices of covolume one the triangular lattice minimizes inverse-power sums (Rankin, Cassels, Ennola, Diananda) and Gaussian theta sums (Montgomery 1988), but these say nothing about non-lattice competitors. Cohn and Kumar (2007, Conjecture 9.4) conjectured that the triangular lattice, like $E_8$ and the Leech lattice, is universally optimal, with sharp Fourier auxiliary functions certifying it; Cohn, Kumar, Miller, Radchenko and Viazovska proved the analogue in dimensions 8 and 24. Does the triangular lattice of covolume one minimize energy per point among all density-one planar configurations, for every completely monotone function $g$ of squared distance?
fields.posedBy: Henry Cohn and Abhinav Kumar (Conjecture 9.4, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 2007)
fields.ageNote: The lattice-only form goes back to Rankin (1953) and Cassels (1959); the conjecture against all configurations is Cohn-Kumar 2007, as cited by the manuscript.
fields.aiRole: The release README says every result in openai/math was produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model with a fixed procedure, on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result. Both manuscripts ship finite checkers (Python, python-flint) for their numerical inputs.

The manuscript states plainly that it does not construct a sharp auxiliary function for each mixed potential, the stronger per-potential quantifier in Cohn-Kumar's Conjecture 9.4; it identifies the minimum value, not all minimizers. fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: the density-one triangular lattice $A$ minimizes the lower energy per point $E_g$ among all locally finite planar configurations of centered-disk density one, for every nonnegative smooth completely monotone $g$ of squared distance, including Gaussians and all inverse powers, with infinite energies allowed and no separation assumption. It does not give a sharp auxiliary function for every mixed potential, does not classify minimizers, and does not treat other dimensions.

fields.name: The Sandier-Serfaty conjecture: the triangular lattice minimizes planar Coulomb renormalized energy
fields.field: Coulomb gases; renormalized energy of Ginzburg-Landau vortex patterns
fields.statement: Sandier and Serfaty introduced a renormalized energy $W$ for infinite configurations of planar point charges against a uniform neutralizing background, defined through curl-free fields $E$ with $\operatorname{div}E=2\pi(\nu-m)$, the logarithmic self-energy removed and energy taken per unit area. It governs microscopic vortex patterns in the Ginzburg-Landau model and limits of two-dimensional Coulomb gases. They proved that a minimum exists, that it is approximated by periodic fields, and that among Bravais lattices the triangular lattice is optimal (Theorems 1 and 2 of their 2012 paper). Their Conjecture 1 asks: is the triangular lattice the minimizer of $W$ over the full admissible class of fields, not only among lattices?
fields.posedBy: Etienne Sandier and Sylvia Serfaty (Conjecture 1, Comm. Math. Phys. 313, 2012)

fields.name: The Brauchart-Hardin-Saff conjecture on the linear term of optimal logarithmic energy on the 2-sphere
fields.field: Discrete energy on the sphere; asymptotics of optimal logarithmic energy
fields.statement: Let $E_{\log}(n)$ be the minimum over $n$ points on the unit sphere $S^2$ of $-\sum_{i\ne j}\log\|y_i-y_j\|$ (Smale's seventh problem concerns near-minimizers). The leading terms $(\tfrac12-\log2)n^2-\tfrac n2\log n$ are classical. Brauchart, Hardin and Saff (2012, Conjecture 4) conjectured that the next term is $C_{\mathrm{BHS}}n+o(n)$ with the explicit constant $C_{\mathrm{BHS}}=2\log2+\tfrac12\log\tfrac23+3\log(\sqrt\pi/\Gamma(1/3))$ coming from the triangular lattice. Betermin and Sandier (2018) proved that the linear coefficient exists and equals this value exactly when the triangular lattice minimizes the planar renormalized energy. Does $E_{\log}(n)=(\tfrac12-\log2)n^2-\tfrac n2\log n+C_{\mathrm{BHS}}n+o(n)$ hold?

fields.name: Sharpness of the Cohn-Elkies linear programming bound in dimension two
fields.field: Discrete geometry; linear programming bounds for packings
fields.statement: Cohn and Elkies (2003) bounded sphere-packing density in $\mathbb R^n$ by any admissible radial $f$ with $f(0)=\widehat f(0)>0$, $\widehat f\ge0$ and $f(x)\le0$ for $|x|\ge r$, giving density at most $\mathrm{vol}(B(0,r/2))$. Numerically the bound appeared to match the best packings in dimensions 2, 8 and 24, and their Conjecture 7.3 asserts that in these dimensions an auxiliary function exists attaining the optimal density exactly. Viazovska (dimension 8) and Cohn-Kumar-Miller-Radchenko-Viazovska (dimension 24) constructed such functions; in the plane the optimal density $\pi/(2\sqrt3)$ is classical (Thue), but no sharp auxiliary function was known. Does an admissible function exist that makes the Cohn-Elkies bound equal to $\pi/(2\sqrt3)$ in dimension two?
fields.posedBy: Henry Cohn and Noam Elkies (Conjecture 7.3, Annals of Mathematics, 2003)

fields.name: Rigidity of the Turing degrees: is every automorphism of the Turing degrees the identity?
fields.field: Computability theory; degrees of unsolvability
fields.statement: The Turing degrees $\mathcal D_T$ are the classes of subsets of $\mathbb N$ under mutual Turing reducibility, partially ordered by $\le_T$. Jockusch and Solovay showed jump-preserving automorphisms fix every degree above $\mathbf 0^{(4)}$; Shore and Slaman showed the jump is definable, so every automorphism preserves it; Nerode and Shore showed each automorphism fixes a cone; and Slaman and Woodin showed every automorphism fixes all degrees above $\mathbf 0''$, that the automorphism group is countable, and that rigidity is equivalent to their biinterpretability conjecture. The rigidity problem asks: is every order automorphism $\pi$ of $(\mathcal D_T,\le_T)$ the identity?

fields.name: The entropy-rate dimension conjecture for self-similar measures on the line (including the exact overlaps conjecture)
fields.field: Fractal geometry; dimension of self-similar measures
fields.statement: Let $\varphi_i(x)=r_ix+t_i$ ($0<|r_i|<1$) be finitely many similarities of $\mathbb R$ and $p$ a positive probability vector, with self-similar measure $\mu=\sum_ip_i(\varphi_i)_*\mu$. Always $\dim_H\mu\le\min\{1,h_{\mathrm{RW}}/\chi\}$, where $h_{\mathrm{RW}}=\lim H(G_n)/n$ is the entropy rate of the random composed map $G_n$ and $\chi=-\sum p_i\log|r_i|$. The exact overlaps conjecture, associated with Simon (1996) and central since Hochman's 2014 work, asks whether equality $\dim_H\mu=\min\{1,H(p)/\chi\}$ holds whenever no two distinct words of equal length give the same map. The entropy-rate dimension conjecture (Varju's survey, Conjecture 3) extends this to systems with exact overlaps. Does $\dim_H\mu=\min\{1,h_{\mathrm{RW}}/\chi\}$ hold for every finite self-similar system on the line?

fields.name: The Global Spherical Shell conjecture for minimal class VII surfaces with positive second Betti number
fields.field: Complex geometry; non-Kahler compact complex surfaces of class VII
fields.statement: A compact complex surface is of class VII if $b_1=1$ and its Kodaira dimension is $-\infty$; these are the non-Kahler surfaces left open by the Enriques-Kodaira classification. fields.statement: Lisonek (2019) called a complex Hadamard matrix $H$ an S-Hadamard matrix if its entrywise square $H^{\circ2}$ is also Hadamard. Tao's cubic matrix of order six, with cube-root-of-unity entries, is an example. Phangara (MSc thesis, Simon Fraser University, 2026, Conjecture 3.1.6) conjectured that it is the only one in order six. Is every S-Hadamard matrix of order six equivalent, under row and column permutations and unit phase multiplications, to Tao's cubic matrix?
fields.posedBy: Jasleen Phangara (Conjecture 3.1.6, MSc thesis, Simon Fraser University, 2026)
fields.aiRole: The release README says every result in openai/math was produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model with a fixed procedure, on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result. This result is not one of the README's two exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region). The manuscript is authored 'OpenAI' and names no human author. The result is Proposition 3.1 of the companion Fourier-certificate manuscript, used there as a lemma.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: Proposition 3.1 of the manuscript was read against Phangara's conjecture as the manuscript quotes it; it states that if $H$ and $H^{\circ2}$ are order-six Hadamard matrices then $H$ is equivalent to Tao's matrix. The proof is a short Newton-identity argument on row ratios. The Lean challenge HadamardCubeFiber formalizes only a supporting cancellation lemma (lean/docs/266.md says so), not this classification, so the entry is Unreviewed. The thesis itself was not opened here.
fields.resultNote: Proposition 3.1: if $H$ and its entrywise square are both complex Hadamard matrices of order six, then $H$ is equivalent to Tao's cubic matrix; in particular all its dephased entries are cube roots of unity. The manuscript notes that uniqueness of the cube-root class was already known from Butson classifications (Lampio-Ostergard-Szollosi; Liang-Chen-Long-Qiu); the new step derives cube-root entries from the two Hadamard conditions for arbitrary phases. It says nothing about other orders.
fields.sourceName: OpenAI math release: Exact Fourier certificates for complex Hadamard matrices of order six
fields.significanceNote: A conjecture from a 2026 master's thesis, settled as a lemma by a short argument and close to known Butson classifications. Placed level with the lowest catalog tier such as Positivity on Deligne-Mumford stacks without the torsion-free hypothesis (5), below Thue-Morse first-occurrence formulas (6).

fields.name: The Erdos-Gallai cycle decomposition conjecture (Erdos Problem #184)
fields.field: Extremal graph theory; graph decompositions
fields.statement: Erdos and Gallai conjectured that the edges of every graph on $n$ vertices can be partitioned into $O(n)$ edge-disjoint cycles and single edges; single edges are needed because forests have no cycles, and $K_{3,n-3}$ shows more than $n$ parts may be necessary. Erdos, Goodman and Posa (1966, Section 5) record the problem and an $O(n\log n)$ bound. Conlon, Fox and Sudakov improved this to $O(n\log\log n)$ (2014) and Bucic and Montgomery to $O(n\log^*n)$; linear bounds were known for random graphs and graphs of linear minimum degree. Is there an absolute constant $C$ such that every $n$-vertex graph decomposes into at most $Cn$ cycles and edges?
fields.posedBy: Paul Erdos and Tibor Gallai, recorded by Erdos, Goodman and Posa (Canad. J. Math. 18, 1966)
fields.aiRole: The release README says every result in openai/math was produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model with a fixed procedure, on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result. This result is not one of the README's two exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region). The manuscript is authored 'OpenAI' and names no human author. The argument builds on the expansion and path-closing methods of Bucic and Montgomery.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: Theorem 1.1 was read against the conjecture and against erdosproblems.com/184; it gives an absolute constant $C$ with every finite simple graph on $n$ vertices partitioned into at most $Cn$ cycles and single edges. The statement ComparatorChallenges/CycleDecomposition.lean was read here: there is a real $C>0$ such that for every $n$ and every SimpleGraph on Fin n there is a $k\le Cn$ and $k$ pairwise disjoint edge sets, each the edge set of a cycle (Walk.IsCycle) or a single edge, whose union is the edge set. This is exactly the headline. Not rebuilt here. Permitted axioms: propext, Quot.sound, Classical.choice.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: an absolute constant $C$ exists such that the edges of every finite simple graph on $n$ vertices partition into at most $Cn$ simple cycles and single edges. Corollary 1.2: every Eulerian graph partitions into at most $Cn$ cycles, and under a quasirandom cut condition into $\Delta/2+\delta n$ cycles. The constant is not computed or optimized; the conjectured sharp values (Erdos suggested $n-1$; $K_{3,n-3}$-type lower bounds of about $3n/2$) are not addressed.
