fields.name: Campana's abelianity conjecture for special compact Kahler manifolds
fields.field: Complex algebraic geometry; fundamental groups of Kahler manifolds
fields.statement: Campana's classification program splits compact Kahler manifolds into special ones and fibrations over orbifold bases of general type. A manifold $X$ is special if it has no Bogomolov sheaf: no line bundle $L\subset\Omega^p_X$ with $\kappa(X,L)=p\ge1$. Rationally connected manifolds, compact tori and manifolds of Kodaira dimension zero are special. Campana (2004, Conjecture 7.1) conjectured that the fundamental group of a special manifold is virtually abelian; Campana and Claudon proved it for threefolds. It would imply, for instance, that every compact Kahler manifold with $\kappa=0$ has virtually abelian $\pi_1$. Is the fundamental group of every special compact Kahler manifold virtually abelian?
fields.posedBy: Frederic Campana (Conjecture 7.1, Ann. Inst. Fourier 54, 2004)
fields.aiRole: The release README says every result in openai/math was produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model with a fixed procedure, on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result. This result is not one of the README's two exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region). The manuscript is authored 'OpenAI' and names no human author. Two companions in the family build on it: 'Two-step monodromy of special quasi-projective varieties' (September 24, 2026), an independent proof of a result the manuscript credits to Cao-Deng-Hacon-Paun, and 'A conditional abelianity theorem for special fourfold pairs with a half-weight divisor' (October 5, 2026), which uses this theorem.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: Theorem 1.1 was read against Campana's Conjecture 7.1 (in the Claudon-Horing appendix form the manuscript cites); it states that every connected smooth compact Kahler manifold that is special has a finite-index abelian subgroup in its full topological $\pi_1$, with no linearity, projectivity or residual finiteness assumption. The proof was not refereed. No Lean formalization of this family is in the release (no lean/docs/057.md at the pinned commit). The manuscript cites another release manuscript (Orbifold and logarithmic Iitaka subadditivity) only to record a known specialness implication, not as a proof input.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: every special compact Kahler manifold has virtually abelian fundamental group, in every dimension. Corollaries: compact Kahler manifolds with $\kappa=0$ have virtually abelian $\pi_1$; Campana's Conjecture S and the bimeromorphic Iitaka uniformization (finite etale covers bimeromorphic to tori when $\gamma d=n$ or the universal cover is $\mathbb C^n$); holomorphic convexity of universal covers of special manifolds. It does not prove the orbifold or quasi-projective versions in general: the companions give a two-step nilpotent bound for linear images in the open case (credited first to Cao-Deng-Hacon-Paun) and one conditional fourfold orbifold case.
fields.sourceName: OpenAI math release: The abelianity conjecture for special compact Kahler manifolds
fields.significanceNote: Campana's abelianity conjecture is a central prediction of his classification program, open since 2004 and known only in dimension three; it contains the long-standing question for Kodaira dimension zero. Placed above the Campana-Peternell conjecture (35) and the projective-base conjecture for Lagrangian fibrations (38), level with the Kuznetsov rationality conjecture (45), below Iitaka's subadditivity conjecture (62).

fields.name: Worst-case Subset Sum in time 2^((1/2 - c)n)
fields.field: Exact exponential algorithms; fine-grained complexity
fields.statement: Given positive integers $a_1,\dots,a_n$ and a target $t$, Subset Sum asks whether some subset of the $a_i$ sums to $t$. The meet-in-the-middle algorithm of Horowitz and Sahni (1974) solves it in time $2^{n/2}\cdot\mathrm{poly}$, and Schroeppel and Shamir (1981) kept that time with space $2^{n/4}$. Later work saved only polynomial factors in the worst case (Chen, Jin, Randolph and Servedio, 2023, time $2^{n/2}/n^{\delta}$), while representation methods beat $2^{n/2}$ only on random instances. Is there an algorithm for worst-case $n$-input Subset Sum running in time $2^{(1/2-c)n}$ for some constant $c>0$?
fields.posedBy: Standing open question of exact exponential algorithms since Horowitz and Sahni (1974); stated as 'a major goal' by Chen, Jin, Randolph and Servedio (2023)
fields.ageNote: The 2^(n/2) barrier dates from Horowitz and Sahni (J. ACM 1974), cited by the manuscript. The manuscript cites no paper that first poses the question; Chen, Jin, Randolph and Servedio (APPROX/RANDOM 2023, cited) call it a major goal of the area in their abstract. Year left blank rather than guessed.
fields.aiRole: The release README says every result in it was produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model following a fixed procedure, on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result, and that some outputs build on earlier model results. This result is not among the README's exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region). The manuscript is authored 'OpenAI' and names no human author. The principal manuscript is dated October 4, 2026; the low-space companion (September 26, 2026) is an earlier, separate result at the 2^(n/2) time scale.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: Theorem 1.1 of the principal manuscript was read against the posed question. It gives a single uniform randomized algorithm, correct with probability at least 2/3 on every input, whose running time is at most $C_c 2^{0.49n}$ on every execution for inputs with bit length $b\le n^c$, on a word RAM with $O(n+b)$-bit words; the intermediate bound is $2^{0.489995n}\mathrm{poly}(n+b)$. The model is stated precisely (no advice, no random oracle, randomness charged). Scope limits stated by the paper: randomized two-sided error (not deterministic), polynomial-bit inputs, word-RAM model. No Lean formalization exists for this family. The proof was not refereed.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: a uniform randomized word-RAM algorithm decides Subset Sum with error at most 1/3 on every input and runs in worst-case time $O(2^{0.49n})$ for every fixed polynomial bound on input bit length, the time bound holding on every random execution. The method combines isolation, a random prime modulus, a filtered Fourier checksum and alias extraction. It is not deterministic, it does not treat super-polynomial bit lengths, and it does not improve the space bound. The companion manuscript separately gives one-sided error, time $\mathrm{poly}(n)2^{n/2}$ and space $O(2^{n/5})$.
fields.sourceName: OpenAI math release: Subset Sum in Time O(2^{0.49n})
fields.significanceNote: Breaking the half-exponent barrier for worst-case Subset Sum is one of the best known open questions of exact exponential algorithms, open since 1974 with only polynomial-factor savings. Placed below the 3SUM hypothesis (50) and the matrix multiplication exponent entry (55), which carry wider downstream consequences, and well above the Bilu-Linial signing conjecture (35).

fields.name: Erdos's question on the maximum modulus of real Littlewood polynomials: is it at least (1 + c) sqrt(N)?
fields.field: Littlewood polynomials; extremal problems on the unit circle
fields.statement: For signs $\epsilon_k\in\{-1,1\}$ let $P(z)=\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\epsilon_k z^k$. Parseval gives $\|P\|_{L^2(|z|=1)}=\sqrt N$, so $\max_{|z|=1}|P(z)|\ge\sqrt N$. Erdos asked whether this is far from sharp: is there an absolute constant $c>0$ with $\max_{|z|=1}|P(z)|\ge(1+c)\sqrt N$ for every such polynomial of large length? The analogue for complex unimodular coefficients was refuted by Kahane's ultraflat polynomials (1980); the Rudin-Shapiro polynomials give $O(\sqrt N)$ and Balister et al. gave two-sided flatness up to constants, but the constant $1+c$ for real signs stayed open. Is $\liminf_N \min_{\epsilon}\max_{|z|=1}|P(z)|/\sqrt N>1$?
fields.posedBy: Paul Erdos
fields.ageNote: Erdos, Some unsolved problems, Michigan Math. J. 4 (1957), Problem 22, as cited by the manuscript; also Hayman-Lingham, Research problems in function theory, Problems 4.13 and 4.31.
fields.aiRole: The release README says every result in it was produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model following a fixed procedure, on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result, and that some outputs build on earlier model results. This result is not among the README's exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region). The manuscript is authored 'OpenAI' and names no human author. The principal manuscript is dated September 23, 2026. Two companions dated October 5, 2026 strengthen it: one adds a lower bound of sqrt(N)/16, the other makes the polynomials two-sided ultraflat; the latter says it reuses lemmas of a 'version-2' refinement of the principal paper.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: Theorem 1.1 ($\lim_N m_N=1$ through all integers $N$) was read against Erdos's real-sign question; it answers it in the negative. lean/formalization.yaml lists a main result for this manuscript (comparator AsymptoticallyMinimalLittlewood, declaration OAI.AsymptoticallyMinimalLittlewood.main). The comparator statement was read here: for every $\eta>0$ there is $N_0$ such that for every $N\ge N_0$ there are real signs with $|\sum_{k<N}\epsilon_k z^k|\le(1+\eta)\sqrt N$ for all $|z|=1$. This states the headline claim exactly. Not rebuilt here. Permitted axioms: propext, Quot.sound, Classical.choice. The proof is existential with no rate or algorithm, as the paper says. The paper says its theorem conflicts with nonflatness claims in preprints of el Abdalaoui (arXiv:1609.03435 and two others) and examines specific issues in those arguments in its Appendix A; no public response to this release was found or searched for here. Listed as Contested because of the conflicting claim described in the claim issue.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: $\min_{\epsilon}\max_{|z|=1}|\sum_{k<N}\epsilon_k z^k|=(1+o(1))\sqrt N$ as $N\to\infty$ through all integers, so no constant $c>0$ as in Erdos's question exists. The construction relaxes to real coefficients in $[-1,1]$ with small defect, using sampled quadratic-phase modes and a hypergraph interval packing, then rounds to signs by a Lovett-Meka partial-coloring argument. It is existential and gives no rate. The principal paper gives no uniform lower bound; the October 5 companions add $|P|\ge\sqrt N/16$ and then full two-sided ultraflatness $(1\pm\epsilon)\sqrt N$ at every large length.
fields.sourceName: OpenAI math release: Asymptotically minimal maxima of real Littlewood polynomials
fields.significanceNote: A 1957 Erdos question at the heart of the Littlewood polynomial literature, sharpened by Kahane's 1980 complex-coefficient answer and listed in Hayman's problem book; well known to harmonic analysts and combinatorialists, with a large computational literature. Placed level with the Artin groups CAT(0) conjecture (40), below Brennan's conjecture (45), and above the Bilu-Linial signing conjecture and Feige's conjecture (both 35).
fields.claimIssueNote: This result conflicts with published claims. Preprints by el Abdalaoui (arXiv:1609.03435 and two others) claim the opposite, that such flat polynomials do not exist; the release's manuscript argues in its Appendix A that those arguments have specific gaps. Until the conflict is settled in public, the entry is Contested.

fields.name: Turyn's conjecture that binary merit factors are bounded
fields.field: Binary sequences; aperiodic autocorrelation
fields.statement: For a binary word $A=(a_0,\dots,a_{N-1})\in\{-1,1\}^N$ with aperiodic autocorrelations $C_u(A)=\sum_{j=0}^{N-1-u}a_ja_{j+u}$, the merit factor is $F(A)=N^2/(2\sum_{u=1}^{N-1}C_u(A)^2)$. Equivalently $1/F(A)=\|P_A\|_4^4/N^2-1$ for the polynomial $P_A(z)=\sum a_jz^j$ on the unit circle. The best proven constructions, from modified Legendre sequences, reach limiting merit factor about $6.34$ (Jedwab, Katz and Schmidt). Turyn's conjecture, equivalently Erdos's $L^4$-norm conjecture, asserts that $F(A)$ is bounded over all binary words of all lengths. Is the merit factor of binary sequences bounded?
fields.posedBy: Richard J. Turyn (name as used by Downarowicz and Lacroix 1998); equivalently Erdos's L4-norm conjecture
fields.ageNote: The manuscript cites Downarowicz and Lacroix (Theoret. Comput. Sci. 1998), who call the boundedness conjecture Turyn's conjecture, equivalently Erdos's L4-norm conjecture. Neither the manuscript nor that citation as quoted gives the year Turyn stated it, so the year is left blank.

This result is not among the README's exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region). The manuscript is authored 'OpenAI' and names no human author. The principal manuscript is dated September 23, 2026. Two companions dated October 5, 2026 strengthen it: one adds a lower bound of sqrt(N)/16, the other makes the polynomials two-sided ultraflat; the latter says it reuses lemmas of a 'version-2' refinement of the principal paper.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: Section 1.2 and Section 8 of the manuscript were read against Turyn's conjecture; the paper claims the largest merit factor at length $N$ tends to infinity through all integer lengths, deduced from flatness in every finite $L^p$ sense. The challenge LittlewoodFiniteFlatness is not in the formalization catalogue (lean/formalization.yaml); it is linked from lean/docs/076.md and its solution module exists at the pinned commit. Its statement was read here: one family of real-sign polynomials, one for each length, with $\int |\,|P_N|/\sqrt N-1|^p\to0$ for every finite $p>0$. This is narrower than the headline: merit factors are not defined in the Lean, and the passage from $p=4$ flatness to unbounded merit factor is a standard identity left informal. Not rebuilt here. The paper says its theorem conflicts with nonflatness claims in preprints of el Abdalaoui (arXiv:1609.03435 and two others) and examines specific issues in those arguments in its Appendix A; no public response to this release was found or searched for here. The construction is existential: no explicit sequences, no rate and no algorithm are given.

fields.name: The periodic tiling conjecture in dimension three
fields.field: Translational tilings of lattices and Euclidean space
fields.statement: A finite nonempty $F\subset\mathbb Z^d$ is a translational tile if $A\oplus F=\mathbb Z^d$ for some $A$; the tiling is periodic if $A$ is invariant under a finite-index subgroup. The periodic tiling conjecture (Lagarias and Wang, 1996, also in a Euclidean form for bounded measurable tiles of $\mathbb R^d$) asserts that every translational tile admits a periodic tiling. It holds in $\mathbb Z$ (Newman) and $\mathbb Z^2$ (Bhattacharya), and Greenfeld and Tao disproved it in sufficiently high dimension. Does every finite translational tile of $\mathbb Z^3$, and every bounded tile of $\mathbb R^3$, admit a periodic tiling?
fields.posedBy: Jeffrey C. Lagarias and Yang Wang
fields.ageNote: Lagarias and Wang, Tiling the line with translates of one tile, Invent. Math. 124 (1996), p. 346, as cited by the manuscript. The dimension-three case became the open frontier after Greenfeld and Tao's high-dimensional counterexample (Annals 2024).
fields.aiRole: The release README says every result in it was produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model following a fixed procedure, on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result, and that some outputs build on earlier model results. This result is not among the README's exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region). The manuscript is authored 'OpenAI' and names no human author. Single-manuscript family dated September 23, 2026. The paper says it follows the Sudoku strategy of Greenfeld and Tao and adds a new encoding keeping the finite factor cyclic.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: Theorem 1.1 was read against the conjecture; it gives a finite tile of $\mathbb Z^3$ that tiles but admits no fully periodic tiling, and its unit-cube thickening has the same property in $\mathbb R^3$ with arbitrary real translations. lean/formalization.yaml lists a main result for this manuscript (comparator PeriodicTilingThree, declaration OAI.PeriodicTilingThree.periodic_tiling_counterexample_and_minimality). The comparator statement was read here: it asserts a nonempty finite $T\subset\mathbb Z^3$ with a tiling and no finite-index-invariant tiling, an almost-everywhere tiling of $\mathbb R^3$ by its thickening with no tiling invariant under a full-rank lattice, and that 3 is the least $d$ admitting such a lattice tile. This states the headline claim, plus minimality. Not rebuilt here. Permitted axioms: propext, Quot.sound, Classical.choice.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: there is a finite nonempty $T\subset\mathbb Z^3$ that tiles $\mathbb Z^3$ by translations, but no translation set of a tiling is invariant under a finite-index subgroup; and $T+[0,1]^3$ tiles $\mathbb R^3$ up to null sets, with no tiling whose translation set is invariant under a full-rank lattice, even allowing real translations. With Bhattacharya's planar theorem, three is the least lattice dimension where periodic tiling fails. The tile is not claimed to be connected, and the result concerns full periodicity only, not the absence of every individual period.
fields.sourceName: OpenAI math release: A translational tile with no fully periodic tiling in dimension three
fields.significanceNote: The periodic tiling conjecture is a well-known tiling problem whose high-dimensional failure was an Annals paper; the remaining low dimensions, with dimension three now the least possible, were the natural open frontier. Placed above the three-dimensional strongly aperiodic monotile question (35), just below the Artin groups CAT(0) conjecture (40), and below whole-conjecture entries such as Brennan's conjecture (45).

fields.name: The complete Crouzeix conjecture: the numerical range is a complete 2-spectral set
fields.field: Matrix analysis; numerical range and spectral sets
fields.statement: For $A\in M_n(\mathbb C)$ with numerical range $W(A)=\{x^*Ax:\|x\|=1\}$ and a matrix polynomial $P(z)=\sum_{j=0}^d B_jz^j$ with $B_j\in M_m(\mathbb C)$, put $P[A]=\sum_j A^j\otimes B_j$. Crouzeix conjectured in 2004 that $\|p(A)\|\le2\max_{W(A)}|p|$ for scalar polynomials (the case $m=1$), and in 2007 proved the complete bound with constant 11.08; Crouzeix and Palencia lowered the complete constant to $1+\sqrt2$. The complete conjecture asks for the constant 2 uniformly in $m$, $n$ and $d$, that is, that $W(A)$ is a complete 2-spectral set. Does $\|P[A]\|\le2\sup_{z\in W(A)}\|P(z)\|$ hold for all such $A$ and $P$?
fields.posedBy: Michel Crouzeix (scalar form 2004; complete form as named in the later literature)
fields.ageNote: The manuscripts date the scalar question to Crouzeix 2004 and his complete bound 11.08 to 2007, and cite Ohag, Czyz and Virtanen (2026) for the name 'complete Crouzeix conjecture', but do not say when the complete form was first stated as a conjecture. Year left blank.
fields.aiRole: The release README says every result in it was produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model following a fixed procedure, on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result, and that some outputs build on earlier model results. This result is not among the README's exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region). The manuscript is authored 'OpenAI' and names no human author. The principal manuscript (September 23, 2026) gives a structural proof via an optimal similarity and a common positive boundary density; a second manuscript (September 26, 2026) gives a separate direct proof of the finite-matrix inequality. The manuscripts cite the scalar proofs of Jin, of Lorist and Schwenninger, and of Luo.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: the complete inequality in Corollaries 6.1 and 6.3 of the principal manuscript and Theorem 1.1 of the direct companion were read against the complete conjecture. lean/formalization.yaml lists main results for both manuscripts (CompleteCrouzeix, DirectCrouzeix, StructuralCrouzeix). The CompleteCrouzeix comparator was read here: for all $n,m\ge1$, $d$, $A\in M_n$ and $B_j\in M_m$, $\|\sum_k A^k\otimes B_k\|\le2\sup_{W(A)}\|\sum_k z^kB_k\|$, and 2 is the least such universal constant. This states the headline claim for matrices. The operator version, challenge CrouzeixHilbert, is not in the formalization catalogue; it is linked from lean/docs/325.md, its solution module exists at the pinned commit, and its statement (arbitrary complex Hilbert space, plus holomorphic and rational extensions and sharpness) was read here. Not rebuilt here.
fields.resultNote: Shown: for every bounded operator $A$ on any complex Hilbert space (no separability assumed) and every matrix polynomial $P$, $\|P[A]\|\le2\sup_{W(A)}\|P\|$, with 2 sharp; the same bound holds for finite matrix-valued functions holomorphic near $\overline{W(A)}$ and for rational functions with poles outside it. fields.name: Stein's conjecture on the Hilbert transform along Lipschitz vector fields
fields.field: Harmonic analysis; directional singular integrals
fields.statement: For a unit vector field $v:\mathbb R^2\to S^1$ consider the truncated directional Hilbert transform $H_{v,a}f(x)=\mathrm{p.v.}\int_{|t|<a}f(x-tv(x))\,dt/t$, which integrates along the line through $x$ in direction $v(x)$. Stein conjectured that Lipschitz regularity suffices: there is an absolute $\epsilon_0>0$ such that, with outer length $a=\epsilon_0/\|v\|_{\mathrm{Lip}}$, $H_{v,a}$ is of weak type $(2,2)$ with a constant independent of $v$. Lacey and Li trace it to Zygmund's question on differentiation along Lipschitz directions; Holder fields of any exponent below one do not suffice. Is $H_{v,a}$ uniformly weak-$(2,2)$ bounded for all Lipschitz unit fields at this scale?

fields.name: Explicit nonbipartite Ramanujan graphs of every degree
fields.field: Spectral graph theory; expanders
fields.statement: A $d$-regular graph is Ramanujan if every nonconstant adjacency eigenvalue $\lambda$ satisfies $|\lambda|\le2\sqrt{d-1}$, the Alon-Boppana optimum. Existence of nonbipartite ones in every degree now follows from random-graph universality (Huang, McKenzie, Yau), but non-constructively. fields.name: The hot spots conjecture for smooth simply connected planar domains
fields.shortName: Hot spots, smooth simply connected planar
fields.field: Spectral theory of the Neumann Laplacian
fields.statement: Rauch's hot spots problem (1975) asks whether an eigenfunction for the first positive Neumann eigenvalue $\mu_1(\Omega)$ of a bounded domain $\Omega$ attains its maximum and minimum only on the boundary. fields.name: The Deligne-Drinfeld conjecture: the Grothendieck-Teichmuller Lie algebra is free on odd generators
fields.field: Grothendieck-Teichmuller theory; multiple zeta values
fields.statement: Let $\mathfrak{grt}_1$ be the graded space of Lie polynomials $\psi(x,y)$ in two letters satisfying antisymmetry, the hexagon (three-term) relation and the pentagon relation in the infinitesimal pure braid Lie algebra $\mathfrak t_4$, with the Ihara bracket. The Deligne-Drinfeld conjecture asserts that $\mathfrak{grt}_1$ is exactly a free Lie algebra with one generator in each odd weight $3,5,7,\dots$. Is $\mathfrak{grt}_1\otimes\mathbb Q$ freely generated by one element in each odd weight at least three?

fields.name: Matiyasevich's single-fold conjecture: every r.e. set has a single-fold Diophantine representation
fields.field: Computability; Hilbert's tenth problem
fields.statement: By the Davis-Putnam-Robinson-Matiyasevich theorem every recursively enumerable set $S\subseteq\mathbb N^n$ has a Diophantine representation: a polynomial $P$ with integer coefficients such that $a\in S$ iff $P(a,w)=0$ for some $w\in\mathbb N^m$. The representation is single-fold if such $w$ is unique when it exists, finite-fold if there are finitely many. Matiyasevich (1974) proved single-fold exponential Diophantine representations and posed the polynomial case, reducing it to a single-fold representation of exponentiation; the finite-fold conjecture is the weaker form. Does every recursively enumerable set have a single-fold Diophantine representation?

fields.ageNote: Matiyasevich, The existence of non-effectivizable estimates in the theory of exponential Diophantine equations, Zap. Nauchn. Sem. LOMI 40 (1974), Section 1; finite-fold form in Matiyasevich, Towards finite-fold Diophantine representations (2010); both cited by the manuscript.

fields.name: The global quantum geometric Langlands conjecture at irrational level
fields.field: Geometric representation theory; geometric Langlands
fields.statement: For a connected simple complex group $G$ with Langlands dual $G^\vee$, lacing number $r$ and a smooth projective curve $X$, let $D_c(\mathrm{Bun}_G(X))$ be the DG category of D-modules on the moduli stack of $G$-bundles twisted by the power of the determinant line corresponding to shifted level $c$. The quantum geometric Langlands conjecture, in Stoyanovsky's inverse-parameter form attributed to Drinfeld and developed in Gaitsgory's quantum Langlands program, predicts an equivalence $D_c(\mathrm{Bun}_G(X))\simeq D_{-1/(rc)}(\mathrm{Bun}_{G^\vee}(X))$ compatible with localization and Whittaker coefficients, deforming ordinary geometric Langlands. Does this equivalence hold for every level $c$, in particular for irrational $c$?
fields.posedBy: A. V. Stoyanovsky (attributing the idea to Drinfeld); developed by Dennis Gaitsgory

fields.name: The combinatorial invariance conjecture for Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials
fields.field: Algebraic combinatorics: Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials and Bruhat order
fields.statement: For a Coxeter system $(W,S)$ with Bruhat order $\le$ and $u\le b$, the Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomial $P_{u,b}(q)$ is defined algebraically, through the Hecke algebra and the simple generators, while the Bruhat interval $[u,b]=\{x:u\le x\le b\}$ is a finite graded poset that remembers neither generators nor root labels. The combinatorial invariance conjecture, attributed to Lusztig and to Dyer, asserts that the polynomial depends only on the interval as an abstract poset. Known before this work: principal lower intervals $[1,b]$ (du Cloux, Brenti, Brenti-Caselli-Marietti, Delanoy), invariance of the coefficient of $q$ (Patimo; Barkley-Gaetz-Lam), and full invariance in interval rank at most six, or up to ten or twelve in some finite Weyl groups. If $[u,b]$ in $(W,S)$ and $[u',b']$ in $(W',S')$ are isomorphic as posets, is $P_{u,b}(q)=P_{u',b'}(q)$?

fields.ageNote: The manuscript attributes the conjecture to Lusztig and Dyer (citing Delanoy 2006) and gives Dyer's 1991 paper as the published formulation, stated there for finite Coxeter systems. fields.name: Thiele's Problem 13: the symmetric L3 bound for the triangular Hilbert transform
fields.field: Harmonic analysis: entangled multilinear singular integrals
fields.statement: For functions $f,g,h$ on the plane, the triangular Hilbert transform is the trilinear form $\Lambda_3(f,g,h)=\mathrm{p.v.}\int_{\mathbb R^3}f(x,y)\,g(y,z)\,h(z,x)\,\frac{dx\,dy\,dz}{x+y+z}$. Each input sees one pair of the three variables and the pairs form a cycle, so it is a basic entangled singular integral; its two-variable analogue is equivalent to the Hilbert transform. Before this work only growing bounds were known: truncations to $1<|x+y+z|<N$ obey $C(\log N)^{1/2}\|f\|_3\|g\|_3\|h\|_3$ (Durcik, Kovac, Thiele), and a dyadic model was bounded only under structural assumptions on one input (Kovac, Thiele, Zorin-Kranich). Thiele's Problem 13: is there a universal constant $C$ with $|\Lambda_3(f,g,h)|\le C\|f\|_{L^3}\|g\|_{L^3}\|h\|_{L^3}$?

fields.name: The classification problem for finite Euclidean Ramsey sets
fields.field: Euclidean Ramsey theory
fields.statement: A finite set $A$ in Euclidean space is Ramsey if for every number of colors $r$ there is a dimension $D$ such that every $r$-coloring of $\mathbb R^D$, with no regularity assumed, contains a monochromatic congruent copy of $A$ at its original scale. Erdos, Graham, Montgomery, Rothschild, Spencer and Straus introduced the notion in 1973 and proved that every Ramsey set is spherical. Known Ramsey sets include nondegenerate simplices (Frankl-Rodl), sets with a soluble transitive isometry group and cyclic trapezoids (Kriz), and vertex sets of regular polytopes (Cantwell). Graham conjectured that every spherical set is Ramsey (1994); Leader, Russell and Walters conjectured that a set is Ramsey exactly when it embeds in a finite transitive set (2012). Which finite sets are Ramsey: is there a necessary and sufficient criterion?

fields.ageNote: The manuscript frames the characterization as the problem of the area since the 1973 paper, with two conjectured answers: Graham's (1994, sphericity) and Leader-Russell-Walters' (2012, subtransitivity). It does not quote an explicit question from the 1973 paper. Graham's conjecture was disproved by Palvolgyi in September 2026, before this manuscript.

fields.name: The Leader-Russell-Walters conjecture: is every Euclidean Ramsey set subtransitive?
fields.field: Euclidean Ramsey theory
fields.statement: A finite set in Euclidean space is Ramsey if for every number of colors $r$ there is a dimension $D$ such that every $r$-coloring of $\mathbb R^D$ contains a monochromatic congruent copy of it. fields.name: The fixed point property for nonexpansive maps in reflexive Banach spaces
fields.shortName: Nonexpansive fixed points in reflexive spaces
fields.field: Functional analysis: metric fixed point theory
fields.statement: A Banach space has the fixed point property for nonexpansive maps if every $T:C\to C$ with $\|Tx-Ty\|\le\|x-y\|$, on every nonempty closed bounded convex set $C$, has a fixed point, nonexpansiveness being measured in the given norm. Browder and Gohde (1965) proved it for uniformly convex spaces and Kirk (1965) for reflexive spaces when the domain has normal structure; Karlovitz showed normal structure is not necessary, Maurey proved it for reflexive subspaces of $L^1$, and Alspach (1981) gave a fixed-point-free nonexpansive map on a weakly compact convex subset of $L^1$, so weak compactness alone does not suffice. Dominguez Benavides showed that every reflexive space has an equivalent norm with the property. Does every real reflexive Banach space have the fixed point property for nonexpansive maps in its original norm?

fields.name: The trilinear Hilbert transform conjecture at the L3 x L3 x L3 to L1 point (slopes 1, 2, 3)
fields.field: Harmonic analysis: multilinear singular integrals
fields.statement: The trilinear Hilbert transform with slopes 1, 2, 3 is $T(f_1,f_2,f_3)(x)=\mathrm{p.v.}\int_{\mathbb R}f_1(x-t)f_2(x-2t)f_3(x-3t)\,\frac{dt}{t}$. Its bilinear predecessor was proved bounded by Lacey and Thiele (1997-1999). In the trilinear case quadratic modulations survive in the associated four-linear form (the coefficients $(-1,3,-3,1)$ annihilate polynomials of degree two), so time-frequency analysis does not close the argument; Tao (2015) obtained only sublogarithmic growth for truncations, and Hu and Lie record the straight-line boundedness problem as open. The standard conjecture asks for bounds $L^{p_1}\times L^{p_2}\times L^{p_3}\to L^r$ over a range of exponents. In particular, is $T$ bounded from $L^3(\mathbb R)\times L^3(\mathbb R)\times L^3(\mathbb R)$ to $L^1(\mathbb R)$?

fields.field: Graph theory: Hamiltonian cycles in planar graphs
fields.statement: A graph is cubic if every vertex has degree three, and polyhedral if it is planar and 3-vertex-connected, that is, the graph of a convex polyhedron. fields.name: C1 regularity of infinity-harmonic functions in dimension three and higher
fields.field: Nonlinear elliptic PDE: the infinity Laplacian
fields.statement: A continuous function $u$ is infinity-harmonic if it is a viscosity solution of $\Delta_\infty u=\sum_{i,j}u_iu_ju_{ij}=0$; by Jensen (1993) and Crandall-Evans-Gariepy (2001) these are the absolutely minimizing Lipschitz extensions studied by Aronsson (1967). Solutions are locally Lipschitz, but the equation controls second derivatives only in the gradient direction, and Aronsson's example $|x_1|^{4/3}-|x_2|^{4/3}$ shows the gradient is at best $C^{0,1/3}$. In the plane, Savin (2005) proved $u\in C^1$ and Evans and Savin (2008) proved $C^{1,\alpha}$; Evans and Smart (2011) proved differentiability at every point in every dimension, which does not give continuity of the gradient. fields.name: The Gaussian moat problem
fields.field: Gaussian primes and sieve methods
fields.statement: A Gaussian prime is an irreducible element of $\mathbb Z[i]$, viewed as a point of the plane. For a step bound $D$, join two Gaussian primes when their distance is at most $D$. Large prime-free disks exist with centers on any line (Gethner, Wagon, Wick), but a walk in the plane can go around them, and computations bound only the component of a particular starting region (Tsuchimura, steps up to 6 from the origin). Gethner and Stark (1997) formulated a version uniform in the starting point and proved it for step bounds $\sqrt2$ and $2$ by periodic sieving. Is it impossible, for every finite $D$, to walk to infinity through distinct Gaussian primes with steps of length at most $D$?

fields.name: Is there an infinite finitely presented simple amenable group?
fields.field: Geometric group theory: amenable and simple groups
fields.statement: A discrete group is amenable if it has Folner sets: for every finite $K\subseteq G$ and $\varepsilon>0$ there is a nonempty finite $D$ with $|gD\,\triangle\,D|<\varepsilon|D|$ for all $g\in K$. Those derived groups are not finitely presented (Matui), and the local embeddability of full groups into finite groups (Grigorchuk-Medynets) explains why such examples cannot be. fields.name: The boundedness and persistence conjectures for weakly reversible mass-action systems
fields.field: Chemical reaction network theory: mass-action kinetics
fields.statement: A reaction network has complexes $y\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^d$ and reactions $y\to y'$; it is weakly reversible if every reaction has a directed return path. With positive rate constants, mass-action kinetics is $\dot x=\sum_{y\to y'}\kappa_{y\to y'}x^y(y'-y)$ on the positive orthant. Feinberg (1987) formulated the expectation that a positive trajectory of a weakly reversible system cannot converge to a point with a zero concentration. Anderson (2011) separated the boundedness conjecture (every positive trajectory is bounded) from the persistence conjecture (no bounded positive trajectory has $\liminf_t x_i(t)=0$). Known cases included one linkage class (Anderson; Gopalkrishnan-Miller-Shiu), two species (Craciun-Nazarov-Pantea) and two-dimensional stoichiometric subspace (Pantea). For weakly reversible mass-action systems with positive constant rates, is every positive trajectory global, bounded and persistent?

fields.name: The permanence conjecture for weakly reversible mass-action systems with fixed rates
fields.field: Chemical reaction network theory: mass-action kinetics
fields.statement: For a weakly reversible reaction network with mass-action kinetics $\dot x=\sum_{y\to y'}k_{y\to y'}x^y(y'-y)$ and fixed positive rates, let $S$ be the span of the reaction vectors $y'-y$ and $P=(c+S)\cap\mathbb R^d_{>0}$ a positive stoichiometric class, which may be unbounded. The system is permanent on $P$ if every solution starting in $P$ is global and positive and one compact $K\subset P$ eventually contains each of them, the entry time but not $K$ depending on the initial point. This is stronger than boundedness plus persistence of each trajectory. Known before: permanence for strongly endotactic networks, including weakly reversible ones with one linkage class (Gopalkrishnan-Miller-Shiu; Boros-Hofbauer), and for two species (Craciun-Nazarov-Pantea). fields.name: Serre's positivity conjecture for intersection multiplicities
fields.field: Commutative algebra; intersection multiplicities over regular local rings
fields.statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a regular local ring of dimension $d$ and $M,N$ finitely generated $R$-modules with $\ell(M\otimes_R N)<\infty$. Serre defined the intersection multiplicity $\chi^R(M,N)=\sum_{i}(-1)^i\,\ell(\mathrm{Tor}_i^R(M,N))$ and conjectured that it vanishes when $\dim M+\dim N<d$, is nonnegative, and is strictly positive when $\dim M+\dim N=d$. Serre proved these in equicharacteristic and in the unramified case; vanishing was proved by Roberts and by Gillet-Soule and nonnegativity by Gabber, while positivity stayed open in ramified mixed characteristic, with special cases by Skalit and by KC-Soto Levins. Is $\chi^R(M,N)>0$ for all nonzero $M,N$ over every regular local ring with $\ell(M\otimes_R N)<\infty$ and $\dim M+\dim N=\dim R$?
fields.posedBy: J.-P. Serre, Local Algebra, Chapter V (cited by the manuscript in the 2000 English translation, Springer Monographs in Mathematics)
fields.ageNote: The manuscript cites Serre's Local Algebra only through its 2000 English translation, so it gives no date for the conjecture itself. The French original (Algebre locale, multiplicites) is a 1960s lecture-notes volume, usually dated 1965; the curator should confirm and set yearPosed.

fields.name: The planar and bounded-treewidth cases of the GNRS L1-embedding conjecture
fields.shortName: GNRS conjecture: planar and bounded treewidth
fields.field: Metric embeddings into L1; multicommodity flow-cut gaps
fields.statement: Gupta, Newman, Rabinovich and Sinclair conjectured that for every proper minor-closed family of graphs there is a constant $C$ such that the shortest-path metric of every graph in the family, with arbitrary positive edge lengths, embeds into $L_1$ with distortion at most $C$; equivalently, the multicommodity flow-cut gap is uniformly bounded on the family. Constant distortion was known for series-parallel graphs (GNRS; sharp value 2 by Chakrabarti-Jaffe-Lee-Vincent) and for bounded outerplanarity, while the best bound for $n$-vertex planar graphs was $O(\sqrt{\log n})$ (Rao 1999). fields.name: Seymour's second neighborhood conjecture
fields.field: Directed graphs; oriented graphs and tournaments
fields.statement: An oriented graph is a finite digraph with no loops, multiple arcs or pairs of opposite arcs. fields.name: Donaldson's tamed-to-compatible conjecture for almost complex four-manifolds
fields.field: Symplectic geometry of four-manifolds; almost complex structures
fields.statement: Let $X$ be a closed smooth four-manifold with a smooth almost complex structure $J$. A symplectic form $\omega$ tames $J$ if $\omega(v,Jv)>0$ for all nonzero tangent vectors $v$, and is compatible with $J$ if moreover $\omega(Ju,Jv)=\omega(u,v)$. Donaldson asked whether a $J$ tamed by some symplectic form must also admit a compatible symplectic form. Known cases: integrable $J$ (complex surfaces, via Buchdahl, Lamari and Li-Zhang), $\mathbb{CP}^2$ (Gromov), generic tamed $J$ when $b_2^+=1$ (Taubes), $S^2\times S^2$ and some rational surfaces (Li-Zhang), and conditional results under $h_J^-=b_2^+-1$. If an almost complex structure on a closed four-manifold is tamed by a symplectic form, is it compatible with some symplectic form?

fields.name: The Schonhage-Strassen conjecture that n log n is optimal for integer multiplication on multitape Turing machines
fields.field: Algorithms; bit complexity of integer multiplication
fields.statement: Schonhage and Strassen (1971) showed that two $n$-bit integers can be multiplied in $O(n\log n\log\log n)$ time on a multitape Turing machine and proposed $n\log n$ as the optimal order of growth. fields.name: Donovan's conjecture on Morita finiteness of blocks with a given defect group
fields.field: Modular representation theory of finite groups; block theory
fields.statement: Let $p$ be a prime and $k$ an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p$ (or, in the integral form, a complete discrete valuation ring $\mathcal O$ with residue field $k$). A block of $kG$ has a defect group, a $p$-subgroup determined up to conjugacy. Donovan's conjecture states that for a fixed finite $p$-group $P$, as $G$ ranges over all finite groups, the blocks with defect group isomorphic to $P$ fall into only finitely many Morita equivalence classes. Known cases include symmetric-group blocks (Scopes), abelian 2-groups (Eaton-Livesey), extraspecial groups of order $p^3$ for $p\ge5$ (An-Eaton) and quaternion defect groups (Eaton-Eisele-Kessar-Linckelmann-Schaeffer Fry, 2026). fields.name: The Abhyankar-Sathaye embedding conjecture
fields.field: Affine algebraic geometry; polynomial automorphisms
fields.statement: A polynomial $f\in\mathbb C[z_1,\dots,z_n]$ is a coordinate if it is the first component of a polynomial automorphism of $\mathbb A^n$. The Abhyankar-Sathaye (epimorphism, or embedding) conjecture asserts that if $\mathbb C[z_1,\dots,z_n]/(f)\cong\mathbb C^{[n-1]}$ then $f$ is a coordinate; geometrically, every hypersurface embedding $\mathbb A^{n-1}\hookrightarrow\mathbb A^n$ is rectifiable. For $n=2$ this is the Abhyankar-Moh-Suzuki theorem; Sathaye and Russell treated planes linear in one variable, and Kaliman-Venereau-Zaidenberg and Maubach handled four-variable equations $a(x)y+b(x,z,t)$. Is every polynomial whose zero locus is isomorphic to affine $(n-1)$-space a coordinate?

fields.name: The stable coordinate conjecture in four variables
fields.field: Affine algebraic geometry; polynomial automorphisms
fields.statement: A polynomial $f\in\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ is a coordinate if some polynomial automorphism sends it to $x_1$, and a one-stable coordinate if it is a coordinate of $\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_n,w]$. fields.name: Is every word-hyperbolic group CAT(0)?
fields.field: Geometric group theory; CAT(0) and CAT(-1) groups
fields.statement: A group is CAT(0) (respectively CAT(-1)) if it acts geometrically, that is properly, cocompactly and by isometries, on a proper complete CAT(0) (respectively CAT(-1)) space. Word-hyperbolic groups are characterised by a linear isoperimetric inequality, a coarse form of negative curvature, and Gromov sought geometric realisations of them by negatively curved spaces. Free groups, closed hyperbolic manifold groups and many cubulated groups are CAT(0); Brady and Crisp found hyperbolic groups with no such action in dimension two. Does every hyperbolic group act geometrically on a proper CAT(0) space, or even a proper CAT(-1) space?

fields.name: The Burr-Erdős hypercube Ramsey conjecture
fields.field: Graph Ramsey theory
fields.statement: Let $Q_n$ be the $n$-dimensional hypercube graph, with $2^n$ vertices, and $R(H)$ the two-colour Ramsey number. Burr and Erdős (1975) called a family of graphs an $L$-set if its Ramsey numbers are bounded by a constant times the order, conjectured that bounded-degeneracy families are $L$-sets (proved by Lee, 2017), and asked separately whether the cubes form an $L$-set. fields.name: The Benjamini-Schramm nonuniqueness conjecture: p_c < p_u for bond percolation on nonamenable quasi-transitive graphs
fields.field: Percolation on nonamenable graphs
fields.statement: Let $G$ be an infinite connected locally finite quasi-transitive graph and consider Bernoulli bond percolation with critical parameter $p_c(G)$ (infinite clusters appear) and uniqueness threshold $p_u(G)$ (the infinite cluster becomes unique almost surely). On a regular tree of degree at least three, $p_c<p_u=1$. Benjamini and Schramm (1996, Conjecture 6) conjectured that nonamenability alone always separates the two thresholds. It was known under extra hypotheses: planar one-ended transitive graphs, highly nonamenable or large-girth graphs, graphs with nonconstant harmonic Dirichlet functions (Gaboriau), Gromov hyperbolic and nonunimodular graphs (Hutchcroft), and Cayley graphs for some suitably chosen generating set. Hutchcroft further conjectured the stronger strict inequality $p_c<p_{2\to2}$ for the $\ell^2$ operator threshold. Is $p_c(G)<p_u(G)$ for every nonamenable quasi-transitive graph $G$, so that some interval of $p$ has infinitely many infinite clusters?

fields.name: The logarithmic Brunn-Minkowski conjecture for origin-symmetric convex bodies
fields.field: Convex geometry; Lp Brunn-Minkowski theory
fields.statement: For origin-symmetric convex bodies $K,L\subset\mathbb R^n$ with support functions $h_K,h_L$ and $0\le\lambda\le1$, the logarithmic combination is the Wulff body $(1-\lambda)K+_0\lambda L=\{x:\langle x,u\rangle\le h_K(u)^{1-\lambda}h_L(u)^\lambda\ \forall u\in S^{n-1}\}$. Boroczky, Lutwak, Yang and Zhang (2012, Problem 1.1) conjectured the log-Brunn-Minkowski inequality $|(1-\lambda)K+_0\lambda L|\ge|K|^{1-\lambda}|L|^\lambda$, which strengthens the multiplicative Brunn-Minkowski inequality and implies the symmetric $L_p$ Brunn-Minkowski inequality for $0<p<1$. They proved it in the plane; it was known for unconditional bodies (Saroglou), bodies with enough common reflection symmetries, complex unit balls, locally near the ball and for zonoids (local form). Does the inequality hold for all origin-symmetric convex bodies in every dimension?

fields.name: The circulant Hadamard conjecture: real circulant Hadamard matrices exist only in orders 1 and 4
fields.field: Design theory; Hadamard matrices and difference sets
fields.statement: A real Hadamard matrix of order $n$ is an $n\times n$ matrix $H$ with entries $\pm1$ and $HH^T=nI_n$; it is circulant if every row is the cyclic shift of the first. Order 4 has the example with first row $(-1,1,1,1)$, and order 1 is trivial. The circulant Hadamard conjecture, traditionally attributed to Ryser (1963), asserts that there are no others. Turyn showed any further order is $4u^2$ with $u$ odd and not a prime power; field descent and later methods of Schmidt and Leung-Schmidt, and the 2017 computation of Logan and Mossinghoff, excluded all but 4489 orders up to $4\cdot10^{30}$. Several claimed proofs have appeared. Is every real circulant Hadamard matrix of order 1 or 4?

fields.name: The Barker-sequence conjecture: no Barker sequence of length greater than 13
fields.field: Sequence design; aperiodic autocorrelation
fields.statement: A Barker sequence of length $n>1$ is a sign sequence $a\in\{-1,1\}^n$ whose aperiodic autocorrelations $C_a(t)=\sum_{j=0}^{n-t-1}a_ja_{j+t}$ satisfy $|C_a(t)|\le1$ for $1\le t<n$. Examples exist at lengths 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 11 and 13. Turyn and Storer (1961) showed that no odd length beyond 13 occurs, and an even length beyond 4 forces all periodic autocorrelations to vanish, that is, a circulant Hadamard matrix of that order. The Barker-sequence conjecture asserts that no Barker sequence of length greater than 13 exists. Is the list $\{2,3,4,5,7,11,13\}$ complete?

fields.name: Yau's nodal-set conjecture for smooth metrics: is nodal measure comparable to sqrt(lambda)?
fields.field: Spectral geometry; nodal sets of Laplace eigenfunctions
fields.statement: Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth closed connected Riemannian manifold of dimension $n$ and $u$ a real eigenfunction, $-\Delta_gu=\lambda u$ with $\lambda>0$. Yau (1982) conjectured that the nodal set $Z_u$ satisfies $c_g\sqrt\lambda\le\mathcal H^{n-1}(Z_u)\le C_g\sqrt\lambda$ with constants depending only on $(M,g)$. Donnelly and Fefferman proved both bounds for real-analytic metrics. For smooth metrics Logunov proved the lower bound in every dimension and a polynomial upper bound; on smooth surfaces the best upper bound was $C\lambda^{3/4-\beta}$ (Logunov-Malinnikova). Does the two-sided bound $\mathcal H^{n-1}(Z_u)\asymp\sqrt\lambda$ hold for every smooth metric, in particular the upper bound?

fields.name: Randomized k-server on arbitrary metrics: a competitive ratio polylogarithmic in k, of optimal order log^2 k
fields.field: Online algorithms; competitive analysis
fields.statement: In the $k$-server problem (Manasse, McGeoch and Sleator, 1988), $k$ servers in a metric space serve online requests, paying the distance moved, against the offline optimum. Against oblivious adversaries the folklore randomized $k$-server conjecture predicted ratio $O(\log k)$ on every metric; Bubeck, Coester and Rabani (2023) refuted it, exhibiting $(k+1)$-point metrics that need $\Omega(\log^2k)$. The best upper bounds depended on the metric: $O(\log^2k\log^3n\log\log n)$ (Bansal-Buchbinder-Madry-Naor), $O(\log^2k)$ on HSTs and hence $O(\log^2k\log n)$ on $n$-point metrics (Bubeck-Cohen-Lee-Lee-Madry); Lee's claimed polylog$(k)$ bound was withdrawn. Is there a randomized algorithm with competitive ratio polylogarithmic in $k$ alone on every metric space, and in particular $O(\log^2k)$?

fields.name: The finite lattice representation problem: is every finite lattice the congruence lattice of a finite algebra?
fields.field: Universal algebra; congruence lattices and subgroup intervals
fields.statement: Gratzer and Schmidt (1963) proved that every algebraic lattice is the congruence lattice of some algebra, but the representing algebra may be infinite even when the lattice is finite. The finite lattice representation problem asks whether every finite lattice $L$ is isomorphic to $\mathrm{Con}(A)$ for some finite algebra $A$ (any finite signature). Palfy and Pudlak (1980) showed this holds for all finite lattices if and only if every finite lattice is an interval $[H,G]$ in the subgroup lattice of a finite group. Positive results cover small lattices and lattices of width at most two, and the decision version (given a lattice table, decide representability) was recorded separately. Is every finite lattice the congruence lattice of a finite algebra?

fields.name: Grothendieck's homotopy hypothesis for weak globular infinity-groupoids (Ara-Henry coherators)
fields.field: Higher category theory; homotopy theory
fields.statement: In Pursuing Stacks (1983) Grothendieck defined weak globular $\infty$-groupoids as models of a coherator, a globular theory obtained by freely adjoining coherence operations, and conjectured that they model homotopy types: their homotopy theory, with weak equivalences detected by components and homotopy groups, is equivalent to that of spaces. Maltsiniotis made the formulation precise; strict $\infty$-groupoids are known to fail. Henry (2016) reduced the hypothesis to a pushout conjecture: attaching an $(n+1)$-cell along the source face of an $n$-cell of a cellular model is a weak equivalence. The case of 3-groupoids was settled by Henry and Lanari. Do Grothendieck $\infty$-groupoids, for every coherator, recover the homotopy theory of spaces?

fields.name: Heilbronn's triangle problem: a power-saving lower bound n^(-2+eta), refuting the almost n^-2 upper bound
fields.field: Discrete geometry; Heilbronn's triangle problem
fields.statement: For $n$ points in the unit square let $\Delta(P)$ be the least area of a triangle they determine, and $\Delta(n)=\max_{|P|=n}\Delta(P)$. Heilbronn asked for the order of $\Delta(n)$, conjecturing $\Delta(n)=O(n^{-2})$ (reported by Roth, 1951); Erdos's parabola gives $\Delta(n)\gg n^{-2}$. Komlos, Pintz and Szemeredi (1982) disproved the conjecture with $\Delta(n)\gg(\log n)/n^2$, and the best upper bound is $n^{-7/6+o(1)}$ (Cohen, Pohoata and Zakharov). The remaining belief, the almost $n^{-2}$ formulation discussed in Zakharov's survey, is that $\Delta(n)\le C_\epsilon n^{-2+\epsilon}$ for every $\epsilon>0$. What is the order of $\Delta(n)$; in particular, is $\Delta(n)=n^{-2+o(1)}$?
fields.posedBy: Hans Heilbronn (reported by K. F. Roth, 1951); the almost n^-2 formulation as discussed in Zakharov's survey
fields.ageNote: Year is that of Roth's paper On a problem of Heilbronn (J. London Math. Soc. 26, 1951), the earliest source the manuscript gives; it does not date Heilbronn's own posing. The almost n^-2 formulation is cited only through Zakharov, Small triangles (J. London Math. Soc. 2026).

fields.name: The Eilenberg-Ganea conjecture
fields.field: Geometric group theory; cohomological and geometric dimension of groups
fields.statement: For a group $G$, the cohomological dimension $\mathrm{cd}\,G$ is the projective dimension of the trivial $\mathbb Z[G]$-module $\mathbb Z$, and the geometric dimension $\mathrm{gd}\,G$ is the least dimension of a $K(G,1)$ CW complex; always $\mathrm{cd}\,G\le\mathrm{gd}\,G$. Eilenberg and Ganea (1957) proved $\mathrm{cd}\,G=\mathrm{gd}\,G$ whenever $\mathrm{cd}\,G\ge3$, and Stallings and Swan settled dimension one. Bestvina and Brady (1997) showed that at least one of the Eilenberg-Ganea conjecture and Whitehead's asphericity conjecture is false, without deciding which. Does every group of cohomological dimension two admit a two-dimensional classifying space?
fields.posedBy: Samuel Eilenberg and Tudor Ganea, On the Lusternik-Schnirelmann category of abstract groups, Ann. of Math. 65 (1957)

fields.name: The generalized Lax conjecture: is every hyperbolicity cone spectrahedral?
fields.field: Real algebraic geometry; hyperbolic polynomials, spectrahedra
fields.statement: A homogeneous real polynomial $p$ is hyperbolic with respect to $e$ if $p(e)\ne0$ and $t\mapsto p(te-x)$ has only real roots for every $x$; its closed hyperbolicity cone is the set of $x$ for which all these roots are nonnegative, a convex cone by Garding. Lax (1958) asked about three variables, and Helton-Vinnikov with Lewis-Parrilo-Ramana showed that every ternary hyperbolic polynomial has a definite determinantal representation. Branden showed that in more variables a hyperbolic polynomial and its powers can fail to be determinantal, which leaves the geometric question about the cone. Is every hyperbolicity cone spectrahedral, that is, of the form $\{x: \sum_i x_iA_i\succeq0\}$ for finitely many real symmetric matrices $A_i$?
fields.posedBy: Generalization of P. D. Lax's 1958 three-variable conjecture; the manuscripts do not name who first stated the general form
fields.ageNote: The manuscripts trace the problem to Lax (1958) and to Helton-Vinnikov (2007) and Lewis-Parrilo-Ramana (2005) for the solved ternary case, but do not attribute the general higher-dimensional conjecture to anyone, so no year is given.

The proof was not refereed. lean/formalization.yaml lists a main result for this manuscript (comparator HyperbolicCones, declaration OAI.Paper256.main_result). ComparatorChallenges/HyperbolicCones.lean was read here: it defines this polynomial on $\mathrm{Sym}_4\times\mathrm{Sym}_4\times\mathbb R^3$, asserts dimension 23, homogeneity of degree 20, $p(e)=1$, real-rootedness along every line, and that for every $N>0$ and every linear map $L$ to $N\times N$ symmetric matrices the cone differs from $\{x:L(x)\succeq0\}$. fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1 (September 24): the degree-20 polynomial $p(X,Z,y)=\det((\det X)Z-\Phi_y(\mathrm{adj}X))$ on $\mathrm{Sym}_4\times\mathrm{Sym}_4\times\mathbb R^3$ is hyperbolic with respect to $(I_4,I_4,0)$, and its closed hyperbolicity cone equals $\{L\succeq0\}$ for no finite real linear pencil $L$. Corollary: the degree-16 quotient $q=p/\det X$ has the same cone. The polynomial is not strictly hyperbolic, consistent with the Kummer-Netzer theorem for strictly hyperbolic polynomials. This cone does have a semidefinite lift with auxiliary variables (companion, October 5); the stronger statement that some hyperbolicity cone has no lift at all is the separate Projected Lax entry.

fields.name: The Projected Lax Conjecture: is every hyperbolicity cone a spectrahedral shadow?
fields.field: Real algebraic geometry; semidefinite lifts of convex cones
fields.statement: A spectrahedral shadow is a set of the form $\{x\in\mathbb R^d:\exists u\in\mathbb R^a,\ A_0+\sum_i x_iA_i+\sum_j u_jB_j\succeq0\}$ with finitely many real symmetric matrices, that is, a set with a finite semidefinite lift. Netzer and Sanyal (2015) proved that a hyperbolicity cone is a spectrahedral shadow when every nonzero boundary point is a smooth point of its hyperbolic polynomial, and formulated the Projected Lax Conjecture, a weakening of the generalized Lax conjecture. Is every closed hyperbolicity cone a spectrahedral shadow?
fields.posedBy: Tim Netzer and Raman Sanyal, Smooth hyperbolicity cones are spectrahedral shadows, Math. Program. 153 (2015)

The proof was not refereed. The construction is nonexplicit (quadratic map with $m=330$, matrix size $20N-1$, $N>10\cdot36^2$) and uses a seed Hankel matrix established by a finite-field certificate in an appendix, which was not re-run here. fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: there exists a real homogeneous hyperbolic polynomial whose closed hyperbolicity cone admits no finite semidefinite lift (exact equality, no closure). The cone comes from a positive semidefinite matrix-valued quadratic map $Q$ via an affine section $E_Q=\{(A,t,y):A\succeq0,\ t\ge\mathrm{tr}(A^\dagger Q(y))\}$, and a local sums-of-squares obstruction in the spirit of Scheiderer rules out every lift. This also disproves the generalized Lax conjecture. It is an existence result in high dimension, not an explicit polynomial and not a lower bound on lift size. Note the explicit cone of the September 24 companion does have an exact lift (size 100 pencil, 307 auxiliary variables).

fields.name: Kaplansky's direct finiteness conjecture
fields.field: Group rings; direct and stable finiteness
fields.statement: A unital ring is directly finite if $ab=1$ implies $ba=1$. For a field $K$ and a group $G$, the group algebra $K[G]$ consists of finite formal sums $\sum c_g g$. In characteristic zero $K[G]$ is directly finite (and stably finite) for every group, by Kaplansky's trace argument. In positive characteristic it was known for free-by-amenable groups (Ara-O'Meara-Perera) and for all sofic groups (Elek-Szabo). Kaplansky asked whether the characteristic-zero theorem persists in positive characteristic. For every field $K$, every group $G$ and all $a,b\in K[G]$, does $ab=1$ imply $ba=1$?

fields.name: Gottschalk's surjunctivity conjecture
fields.field: Symbolic dynamics on groups; cellular automata
fields.statement: For a group $G$ and a finite alphabet $A$, a cellular automaton on $A^G$ is a map $\tau(x)(g)=\phi((x(gu))_{u\in M})$ given by a finite memory set $M\subset G$ and a local rule $\phi:A^M\to A$. $G$ is surjunctive if every injective cellular automaton on $A^G$, for every finite $A$, is surjective. Gromov and Weiss proved that sofic groups are surjunctive, and surjunctivity implies Kaplansky's direct finiteness over finite fields. Gottschalk (1973) conjectured that every group is surjunctive. Is every group surjunctive?
fields.posedBy: Walter Gottschalk, Some general dynamical notions, Recent Advances in Topological Dynamics, LNM 318 (1973)

fields.name: The group-ring Determinant Conjecture (Luck)
fields.field: L2-invariants; Fuglede-Kadison determinants over group von Neumann algebras
fields.statement: For a discrete group $G$ and a matrix $A$ over $\mathbb Z[G]$, let $T_A$ act on $\ell^2(G)^n$ by the regular representation and let $\mu_A$ be the spectral measure of $T_A^*T_A$ with respect to the group trace. A nonsingular integer matrix has $|\det|\ge1$; the Determinant Conjecture (Luck 2002, Conjecture 13.2) asks for the analogue $\int_{(0,\infty)}\log t\,d\mu_A(t)\ge0$, which for invertible $A$ says the Fuglede-Kadison determinant is at least $1$. It was known for amenable groups (Schick) and sofic groups (Elek-Szabo), and underlies approximation and torsion results for $L^2$-invariants. Does the Determinant Conjecture hold for every group?
fields.posedBy: Wolfgang Luck, L2-Invariants: Theory and Applications to Geometry and K-Theory (2002), Conjecture 13.2

The proof was not refereed; it depends on the characteristic-two companion (also Lean-checked). lean/formalization.yaml lists a main result for this manuscript (comparator GroupRingDeterminant, declaration OAI.GroupRingDeterminant.main). This states the headline for invertible matrices, the case that disproves the conjecture; the spectral-integral reformulation is not included. Not rebuilt here.

fields.name: The odd regular two-dimensional Fontaine-Mazur conjecture over Q at p = 2
fields.field: Galois representations; modularity lifting at p = 2
fields.statement: The Fontaine-Mazur conjecture (1995) predicts that irreducible $p$-adic Galois representations unramified outside finitely many primes and de Rham at $p$ come from algebraic geometry. For odd two-dimensional representations of $G_{\mathbb Q}$ with distinct Hodge-Tate weights it takes the form of modularity up to Tate twist. Building on Kisin and Emerton, Pan (2022) and Zhang (2025) established this for every odd prime, and at $p=2$ Tung removed local restrictions only under a nonsolvable residual image. Let $r:G_{\mathbb Q}\to\mathrm{GL}_2(\overline{\mathbb Q}_2)$ be continuous, irreducible, odd, unramified outside finitely many primes, and de Rham at $2$ with distinct Hodge-Tate weights. Is $r$ a Tate twist of the Galois representation of a classical cuspidal eigenform, with no condition on the residual representation?
fields.posedBy: Jean-Marc Fontaine and Barry Mazur, Geometric Galois representations (1995); the p = 2 two-dimensional case is the part left open after Pan and Zhang, as the manuscript explains
fields.aiRole: The release README says the results were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model with a fixed procedure, on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result, and that some outputs build on earlier model results. This result is not among the README's exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region). The manuscript is authored 'OpenAI' and names no human author. The manuscript says this theorem supplies the weight-two modularity input to the release's Hilbert's tenth problem over Q manuscript. It cites several 2025-2026 works (Thorne, Zhang, Emerton-Gee-Pan-Zhu, Pan) as inputs.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: Theorem 1.1 of the September 23 manuscript was read against the odd regular two-dimensional case of the Fontaine-Mazur conjecture as the paper formulates it; it claims modularity up to Tate twist for every such 2-adic representation, including scalar and reducible residual representations. The proof was not refereed. It depends on recent external results whose status was not checked here, notably Thorne's modularity of ordinary weight-{0,1} representations (cited as 2026), Zhang (2025), Pan (2022), Paskunas-Tung (2021) and the release's own companion results. No Lean formalization exists for this family.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: every continuous, irreducible, odd $r:G_{\mathbb Q}\to\mathrm{GL}_2(\overline{\mathbb Q}_2)$ unramified outside finitely many primes and de Rham at $2$ with distinct Hodge-Tate weights is a Tate twist of the representation of a classical cuspidal eigenform; no residual hypothesis. With the odd-prime results this gives the regular odd two-dimensional case over $\mathbb Q$ at every prime. It does not address equal Hodge-Tate weights, even representations, higher dimension or other number fields, so the general Fontaine-Mazur conjecture stays open. Companions prove 2-adic pro-modularity without a de Rham hypothesis (October 4) and Emerton's dimension conjecture at $p=2$ (October 5), entered separately.

fields.name: Emerton's dimension conjecture for the full Hecke algebra at p = 2 and odd level
fields.field: p-adic families of modular forms; Hecke algebras
fields.statement: For a prime $p$ and level $N$ prime to $p$, let $\mathbb T_p(N)$ be the inverse limit over $k$ of the $\mathbb Z_p$-Hecke algebras generated by $T_\ell$ and $\ell S_\ell$ ($\ell\nmid pN$) acting on all modular forms of weights $1,\dots,k$ and level $\Gamma_1(N)$, Eisenstein forms included. Emerton, in his 2011 Bourbaki account of $p$-adic families (Conjecture 2.9), conjectured that every irreducible component of $\mathrm{Spec}\,\mathbb T_p(N)$ has Krull dimension four, and proved the lower bound (Corollary 2.28). For $p=2$ and every odd $N$, does every irreducible component have dimension exactly four?

fields.aiRole: The release README says the results were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model with a fixed procedure, on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result, and that some outputs build on earlier model results. fields.name: Pro-modularity at p = 2: odd absolutely irreducible 2-adic representations occur in the completed Hecke algebra (auxiliary tame level allowed)
fields.field: Completed Hecke algebras; p-adic Langlands for GL2 over Q
fields.statement: Let $\mathbb T_p(N)$ be the full varying-weight $p$-adic Hecke algebra of tame level $N$. Emerton (2011, Conjecture 2.12) records the expectation that every continuous odd two-dimensional $p$-adic representation of $G_{\mathbb Q}$ unramified outside finitely many primes occurs in such an algebra, with no Hodge-theoretic condition at $p$ and with tame level prescribed by the ramification. Earlier pro-modularity theorems (Skinner-Wiles, Emerton, Pan) need $p>2$ or residual restrictions. For $p=2$, does every continuous, odd, absolutely irreducible $r:G_{\mathbb Q}\to\mathrm{GL}_2(E)$ unramified outside finitely many primes occur in $\mathbb T_2(N)$ for some odd $N$?

fields.name: Three-machine unit-job scheduling with precedence constraints (Garey-Johnson OPEN8): is P3|prec,p_j=1|Cmax in P?
fields.field: Scheduling theory; computational complexity
fields.statement: Given a directed acyclic graph on $n$ unit-length jobs and a deadline $T$, can the jobs be scheduled on $m$ identical machines, at most $m$ per time slot, so that every precedence $u\to v$ has $u$ strictly before $v$ and all jobs finish by $T$? For $m=2$ this is polynomial (Fujii-Kasami-Ninomiya 1969, Coffman-Graham 1972); with $m$ part of the input it is NP-complete (Ullman 1975). The fixed case $m=3$, $P3\mid\mathrm{prec},p_j=1\mid C_{\max}$, is listed as open problem OPEN8 in Garey and Johnson's book; the best exact algorithm known ran in time $2^{O(\sqrt n\log n)}$ (Nederlof-Swennenhuis-Wegrzycki). Is three-machine unit-job scheduling with precedence constraints solvable in polynomial time, or is it NP-complete?
fields.posedBy: Michael R. Garey and David S. Johnson, Computers and Intractability (1979), Appendix A13, OPEN8
fields.aiRole: The release README says the results were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model with a fixed procedure, on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result, and that some outputs build on earlier model results. The proof was not refereed. The challenge is not in the formalization catalogue (lean/formalization.yaml); it is found through lean/docs/124.md, and its solution module OAI.Computability.Scheduling.Main exists at the pinned commit. The statement ComparatorChallenges/ThreeMachine.lean was read here: it encodes instances and answers as bit strings and asserts one fixed multitape machine and constant $C$ such that, for every nonempty acyclic instance and every deadline option with $1\le T\le n$, the machine halts within $C(L+2)^{150020}$ steps with a correct output (an optimal schedule, or a feasible schedule or a correct 'infeasible'). This states the headline claim, polynomiality included. Not rebuilt here.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: a uniform deterministic algorithm constructs a minimum-makespan schedule for unit-length jobs with arbitrary precedence constraints on three identical machines, and decides feasibility for a deadline $1\le T\le n$ exactly, in $O((L+2)^{150020})$ Turing machine steps. The method decomposes schedules into gaps whose job sets have bounded-size global Boolean descriptions and searches them by dynamic programming. The exponent is astronomically large and no practical claim is made. It does not settle $m\ge4$ fixed machines, which remains open.

fields.name: The Rohde-Schramm conjecture: critical square-lattice FK interfaces converge to SLE for 1 <= q < 4 (and 0 < q < 1 in smooth domains)
fields.field: Statistical mechanics; random-cluster model, SLE and CLE scaling limits
fields.statement: In the random-cluster (FK) model on the square lattice with cluster weight $q$ at the self-dual point $p_q=\sqrt q/(1+\sqrt q)$, the Dobrushin interface in a domain with two marked boundary points is expected to have a conformally invariant scaling limit. Rohde and Schramm (2005, Conjecture 9.7), restated by Schramm (ICM 2006, Problem 2.6), conjectured for every fixed $0<q<4$ that it converges to chordal $\mathrm{SLE}_{\kappa}$ with $\kappa=4\pi/\arccos(-\sqrt q/2)$. Before this work it was proved only for $q=2$ (FK-Ising, Smirnov and Chelkak-Smirnov) and, for site percolation on the triangular lattice, the analogous $q=1$ statement. Does the critical square-lattice FK interface converge to $\mathrm{SLE}_{\kappa(q)}$ for every $0<q<4$?
fields.posedBy: Steffen Rohde and Oded Schramm, Basic properties of SLE, Ann. of Math. 161 (2005), Conjecture 9.7; Schramm, ICM 2006 (2007), Problem 2.6
fields.aiRole: The release README says the results were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model with a fixed procedure, on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result, and that some outputs build on earlier model results. Two September 23 manuscripts cover $1\le q<4$ and $0<q<1$; October 5 companions extend to $q=4$ and add disordered, thermal (massive) and natural-parametrization results.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: Theorem 1.1 of the September 23 manuscript was read against Rohde-Schramm Conjecture 9.7 as the papers cite it. For $1\le q<4$ it claims convergence in every bounded Jordan domain under uniform marked-boundary approximation (including the square), plus nested whole-plane CLE convergence. The companion for $0<q<1$ proves the smooth-Jordan-domain form and states that Rohde-Schramm's unit-square formulation has different boundary regularity and is not covered; that is why this entry is Partial. The proofs were not refereed. They use recent inputs including Duminil-Copin-Kozlowski-Krachun-Manolescu-Oulamara rotational invariance (cited as 2026). No Lean formalization exists for this family.
fields.resultNote: For every fixed $1\le q<4$ (September 23), and $1\le q\le4$ (October 5 companion), critical square-lattice FK Dobrushin interfaces converge to chordal $\mathrm{SLE}_{\kappa(q)}$ in every bounded Jordan domain with uniformly approximated marks, and the complete nested loop collection of the free infinite-volume measure converges to whole-plane $\mathrm{CLE}_{\kappa(q)}$, keeping multiplicities and traversals. For $0<q<1$ the interface converges to $\mathrm{SLE}_\kappa$, $\kappa\in(6,8)$, in smooth Jordan domains only. No uniformity in $q$ is asserted. Not covered: $0<q<1$ in nonsmooth domains such as the square, CLE for $q<1$, and other lattices.

fields.name: Cardy's formula and conformal invariance for critical bond percolation on the square lattice
fields.shortName: Cardy's formula on the square lattice
fields.field: Percolation; conformal invariance
fields.statement: Cardy (1992) predicted that for critical two-dimensional percolation the probability of an open crossing between two boundary arcs of a conformal quadrilateral converges to an explicit conformally invariant function, $\int_0^x[t(1-t)]^{-2/3}dt\,/\int_0^1[t(1-t)]^{-2/3}dt$ in the half-plane coordinate $x$. Smirnov (2001) proved it for site percolation on the triangular lattice, and Camia-Newman built the full loop limit there, but the proof uses the lattice's special symmetry. For the most standard model, bond percolation on $\mathbb Z^2$ at $p=1/2$, only partial or disputed claims existed. Does Cardy's formula, and conformal invariance of the exploration interface (convergence to $\mathrm{SLE}_6$), hold for critical bond percolation on the square lattice?

fields.name: The near-boundary Birkhoff conjecture: billiards integrable near the boundary are ellipses
fields.field: Dynamical systems; convex billiards and integrability
fields.statement: In a planar billiard in a strictly convex domain $\Omega$, a caustic is a curve such that a trajectory tangent to it stays tangent after every reflection. Ellipses are integrable: confocal ellipses foliate a neighbourhood of the boundary by caustics. The Birkhoff conjecture, traditionally attributed to Birkhoff and first printed by Poritsky (1950), asserts that every integrable strictly convex billiard is an ellipse. Lazutkin found a Cantor family of caustics near the boundary for every smooth positively curved table; Bialy proved rigidity under integrability of the whole phase space; Avila-De Simoi-Kaloshin and Kaloshin-Sorrentino proved local versions near ellipses. Is a smooth, strictly convex, positively curved billiard table an ellipse whenever it is integrable near the boundary?
fields.posedBy: Traditionally attributed to G. D. Birkhoff (Dynamical Systems, 1927); first printed formulation by Hillel Poritsky, Ann. of Math. 51 (1950), as the manuscripts cite
fields.ageNote: The manuscripts attribute the conjecture to Birkhoff and cite his 1927 book for the setting, with Poritsky's 1950 paper as the early printed formulation; the near-boundary form is not attributed to a separate poser.
fields.aiRole: The release README says the results were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model with a fixed procedure, on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result, and that some outputs build on earlier model results. fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: Theorem 1.1 of each September 24 manuscript was read against the Birkhoff conjecture as the papers state it. One proves the ellipse conclusion when a full neighbourhood of the boundary is continuously foliated by smooth closed convex caustics; the other derives such a collar from a continuous foliation of a grazing phase annulus by invariant essential curves, and invokes the first. The proofs were not refereed. Scope stated by the papers: $C^\infty$ boundary with positive curvature, a full collar (a Cantor family of caustics does not suffice), no assumption on dynamics away from the boundary. No Lean formalization exists.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1 (phase foliations): if a $T$-invariant open annulus containing $(\mathbb R/L\mathbb Z)\times(0,\eta)$ in the billiard phase space is homeomorphically foliated by individually invariant essential curves, then $\Omega$ is an ellipse. The companion proves the same conclusion from a continuous collar of smooth closed convex caustics, via analytic regularity of the boundary and complex continuation. Only continuity across leaves is assumed. Not covered: integrability only on a Cantor set, rational integrability, or integrability away from the boundary; the full Birkhoff conjecture (global integrability as typically defined) is reduced to but not identical with this case.

fields.name: The Euclidean Steinitz-Bergstrom conjecture: is the Euclidean Steinitz constant O(sqrt d)?
fields.field: Discrepancy theory; rearrangements of vector sums
fields.statement: Let $S_2(d)$ be the least number such that every finite family of vectors $v_1,\dots,v_N$ in the Euclidean unit ball of $\mathbb R^d$ with $\sum v_i=0$ has an ordering whose partial sums all have norm at most $S_2(d)$. Steinitz's lemma gives a bound depending only on $d$; Grinberg and Sevastyanov (1980) proved $S\le d$ for every norm, and the simplex example shows $S_2(d)\ge\tfrac12\sqrt d$. The expected square-root scale in Euclidean space was discussed by Behrend (1954), and the conjecture is attributed to Bergstrom. Is $S_2(d)=O(\sqrt d)$?
fields.posedBy: Attributed to Viktor Bergstrom (attribution recorded by Ambrus and Heck, Mathematika 2026, Conjecture 5); square-root growth discussed by F. A. Behrend (1954)
fields.ageNote: The manuscript cites Behrend (1954, p. 108) for the expected square-root growth and Ambrus-Heck for the attribution to Bergstrom; Bergstrom's 1931 paper is in its bibliography but is not cited in the text, so 1954 is the earliest dated statement the paper itself relies on.

fields.name: Prescribed-order Euclidean prefix discrepancy O(sqrt d), independent of length (Bansal-Jiang-Meka-Singla-Sinha Conjecture 6.3)
fields.field: Discrepancy theory; vector balancing
fields.statement: Given vectors $v_1,\dots,v_N$ in the Euclidean unit ball of $\mathbb R^d$ in a fixed order, choose signs $\varepsilon_i\in\{\pm1\}$ to keep every prefix sum $\sum_{i\le k}\varepsilon_iv_i$ small. Banaszczyk proved a bound $O(\sqrt d+\sqrt{\log N})$, which grows with the length when $N$ is large compared with $d$. Bansal, Jiang, Meka, Singla and Sinha (2021, Section 6, Conjecture 6.3), following Banaszczyk, conjectured the length-free square-root bound. Is there an absolute $C$ such that every such sequence has signs with all prefix sums of norm at most $C\sqrt d$?

fields.name: Tingley's problem: does every surjective isometry between unit spheres of Banach spaces extend to a linear isometry?
fields.field: Functional analysis; geometry of Banach spaces
fields.statement: For a real normed space $X$ let $S_X$ be its unit sphere with the inherited metric. Mazur and Ulam (1932) proved that surjective isometries between real normed spaces are affine, but a unit sphere has empty interior, so this does not apply. Tingley (1987) asked whether every surjective isometry $f:S_X\to S_Y$ between unit spheres of real Banach spaces extends to a real-linear isometry of $X$ onto $Y$. Positive answers were known for many classical spaces ($C_0$, $L^p$, von Neumann algebras and their preduals, unital $C^*$-algebras) and for every two-dimensional space (Banakh 2022), but not in general, even in finite dimension. Does every surjective isometry between the unit spheres of two real Banach spaces extend to a surjective real-linear isometry?
fields.posedBy: Daryl Tingley, Isometries of the unit sphere, Geometriae Dedicata 22 (1987)

fields.name: Lech's multiplicity conjecture
fields.field: Commutative algebra; Hilbert-Samuel multiplicity
fields.statement: For a nonzero Noetherian local ring $(A,\mathfrak a)$ of dimension $d$, the Hilbert-Samuel multiplicity is $e(A)=\lim_N d!\,\ell_A(A/\mathfrak a^N)/N^d$. Lech (1960) proved the inequality below when the source has dimension at most two and in complete-intersection cases; Ma proved it in equal characteristic for dimension three, for standard graded sources over perfect fields, and a bound $e(R)\le\max\{1,d!/2^d\}e(S)$. Lech asked whether multiplicity can decrease under flat maps. If $(R,\mathfrak m)\to(S,\mathfrak n)$ is a flat local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings, is $e(R)\le e(S)$?
fields.posedBy: Christer Lech, Note on multiplicities of ideals, Ark. Mat. 4 (1960); Inequalities related to certain couples of local rings, Acta Math. 112 (1964)
fields.aiRole: The release README says the results were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model with a fixed procedure, on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result, and that some outputs build on earlier model results.
